Unified company lookup by exact identifier: one call, one normalized schema across French SIREN (recherche-entreprises Sirene/RNE), EU VAT (VIES validation), and global LEI (GLEIF). Returns legal name, status, address, activity code, officers, and full provenance (source, retrieval time, license). No per-register API-key signup — pay once, get consistent company data for e-invoicing, procurement, and compliance. Input: id + id_type (siren | vat | lei).

Entity resolution for KYC/KYB, supplier and customer onboarding and France 2026 e-invoicing: use when you hold a company name, brand or director and need a certain identifier. Returns the French SIREN, EU VAT or global LEI with a confidence score and ranked candidates, cross-checked across official registers (recherche-entreprises Sirene/RNE, GLEIF LEI, EU VIES VAT). Input: name or vat, optional country, director, city.

Complete crypto and DeFi snapshot in ONE call for AI agents: spot prices for your tokens, full market data (market cap, 24h volume, supply, 24h change) for the lead token, top-10 chains by TVL, and the best yield pools by APY. Prices, market, TVL and yields together — the most complete crypto+DeFi call per request.

Crypto market data for AI agents: market capitalization, 24-hour trading volume, 24h percent change, circulating and total supply, and market-cap rank for any coin. Query by Coinpaprika id (btc-bitcoin) or common ticker (btc, eth, sol). One call, USD-denominated, keyless.

Real-time crypto token spot prices for AI agents and trading bots. Returns USD price, token symbol, and DefiLlama price confidence per coin. Query by DefiLlama coin key (coingecko:ethereum) or common ticker (btc, eth, sol, usdc, usdt) — batch up to 50 coins in one call. Keyless, unified schema, stablecoin-payable.

DeFi TVL (total value locked) for AI agents. Query a single protocol by slug (aave, uniswap, lido) for its current USD TVL, a specific chain by name, or omit both for the top 20 chains ranked by TVL. Sourced from DefiLlama — on-chain liquidity and DeFi health signal in USD.

DeFi yield and APY data for AI agents and yield optimizers. Thousands of liquidity and lending pools across chains and protocols, filterable by chain, project, token symbol, minimum TVL and stablecoin-only, sorted by APY. Each pool returns chain, project, symbol, TVL and APY. Sourced from DefiLlama yields.

Forward geocoding for AI agents: turn a place name or address into coordinates. Returns the best-match latitude, longitude, country and ISO country code, administrative regions (admin1/admin2), population, IANA timezone and GeoNames feature code. Query by q= or address=. Sourced from Open-Meteo geocoding — keyless, unified schema, stablecoin-payable.

Place search / geocoding autocomplete for AI agents: return the top matching places for a name query. Each result carries name, latitude, longitude, country and ISO code, administrative regions, population, timezone and feature code. Query by q= with an optional count= (1-20, default 5). Sourced from Open-Meteo geocoding — keyless, unified schema.

Reverse geocoding for AI agents: turn a latitude/longitude into a human-readable address. Returns city, locality, principal subdivision (state/region), country and ISO country code for the given coordinates. Query by lat= and lon=. Sourced from BigDataCloud — keyless, unified schema, stablecoin-payable.

Sanctions screening for compliance, AML, KYC and KYB agents: use before onboarding, paying or contracting with a person or organization. Fuzzy-matches the name against the official OFAC SDN list and the UN Security Council consolidated list, aliases included, and returns scored matches with list, sanctions program, entity type and source reference. Diacritic- and case-insensitive, tunable min_score (default 0.6). One keyless USDC call.

XBRL company financial facts from SEC EDGAR for AI agents and fundamental-analysis bots. Query by stock ticker or CIK for reported us-gaap concepts — revenues, net income, assets, liabilities, EPS and more — each with its latest value, unit, fiscal year and period, form and period-end date. Optionally filter to one concept. Keyless, USD, unified schema.

Recent SEC EDGAR filings for any US public company, for AI agents and research bots. Query by stock ticker or CIK, optionally filter by form type (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K), and get each filing's form, filing date, accession number, primary document and a direct SEC Archives URL. Sourced from SEC EDGAR submissions — keyless, unified schema.

Resolve a US public company's SEC EDGAR CIK for AI agents and financial bots. Look up by stock ticker (AAPL, NVDA, MSFT) or by company name and get the zero-padded 10-digit CIK identifier, ticker, and official registrant title. The keyless first step before any SEC filings or XBRL financial-facts query. Unified schema, stablecoin-payable.

Soil and agriculture intelligence for grower, agronomist and farming agents at any lat/lon. Returns live soil moisture at four depths, soil temperature at 0/6/18/54 cm, reference evapotranspiration (ET0), vapour pressure deficit and frost risk. For irrigation scheduling, soil-health monitoring and crop management.

Air quality, pollution and environmental data for any city or lat/lon. Returns European and US AQI (air quality index), particulate matter PM2.5 and PM10, ozone (O3), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), sulphur dioxide (SO2), and carbon monoxide (CO). Real-time index for health, allergy, pollution-monitoring and environmental agents.

Complete weather bundle in one call: current conditions (temperature, feels-like, humidity, wind speed/direction/gusts, pressure, cloud cover, precipitation, UV, day/night) plus 24-hour hourly and 7-day daily forecast, air quality (AQI, PM2.5, PM10, ozone), solar radiation, and severe-weather alerts. Query by city name or lat/lon. Times in the location local timezone. Most complete weather data per call.

River discharge and flood-risk forecast (Copernicus GloFAS, 5 km grid) for the nearest river to any lat/lon. Returns current river discharge in cubic meters per second (m3/s) plus mean, median, max, min and 25/75 percentiles. Hydrology and natural-disaster data for flood forecasting, insurance, agriculture and river logistics.
Historical daily weather (archive): temperature min/max, precipitation, conditions for a past date range. City or lat/lon. start/end optional — defaults to last 7 complete UTC days.

Marine weather and sea-state forecast for any coastal coordinate. Returns significant wave height, wave direction and period, wind waves, swell (height, direction, period) and ocean current velocity and direction. Oceanographic conditions for shipping, offshore, maritime safety, fishing, surfing and coastal operations.

Current weather right now, cheap: temperature, feels-like, humidity, wind speed and direction, pressure, cloud cover, precipitation, UV, day/night — plus a live air-quality snapshot (AQI, PM2.5) and today’s high/low. City or lat/lon. The budget "weather now" call.

Solar radiation and irradiance forecast for any lat/lon. Returns shortwave (global horizontal) and direct radiation in W/m2 and sunshine duration. For solar energy production forecasting, photovoltaic (PV) yield estimation and renewable-energy planning agents.

Tide predictions and sea-level forecast for any coastal location: hourly sea-level height (meters) plus derived high and low tide times, next 24 hours by default. From Open-Meteo Marine. For shipping, fishing, surfing, and coastal or port operations that need tide tables.

Load a reloadable card balance with USDC. Pay from either chain: the card issuer only accepts USDC on Base, and Laso bridges the payment to the account holder's own deposit address at the issuer over CCTP, which mints native USDC so the full amount arrives. Laso absorbs the bridge cost, so the price is exactly the amount that lands on the balance. Requires a linked card issuer account. Follow with POST /create-reloadable-card to create a card against the balance.

Order an international non-reloadable prepaid card (USD). The order is queued and fulfilled by an admin, after which the card details are retrievable via GET /get-card-data with card_type="Non-Reloadable International". A 3.8% fee is added on top of the on-card amount, or less while a fee promotion is running; the 402 challenge carries the exact total. Submit a whole dollar on-card amount.

Send dollars to a bank account by ACH. Requires a bank destination registered beforehand with addBankingDestination (list them at GET /bank-recipients), which in turn requires an approved banking profile. A payout that cannot be fulfilled returns an error and the x402 payment does not settle, so the USDC stays in the wallet and the agent can retry.

Send a payment via Venmo or PayPal. Requires KYC verification on the calling wallet; if not yet verified the response returns a kyc_url instead of sending the payout. The on-chain x402 payment credits the user's account balance via the standard deposit webhook, so abandoned/unverified flows can be recovered with POST /withdraw.

raw.title: [P2][Combat/DB] Route weapon-RPC kills through execute_death_pipeline, remove combat_runtime writer-reentrancy wipe, and detect same-lock rank-60 recursion
raw.body:
Consolidates three confirmed `P2` combat/concurrency defects (`EP-12`, `EP-13`, `NEW-05`) on `main` (`4d49958c4`).

## Confirmed Defects & Evidence

1. **Weapon-RPC ship kills bypass `execute_death_pipeline` across split transactions (`EP-13`):**
   - Direct weapon-RPC ship kills (`services/combat_weapons.rs:1447-1466`, `services/combat_weapons_spool.rs:224-640`, `services/combat_wrecks_killmails.rs:309-416`) run a separate multi-transaction kill path instead of `combat/death_pipeline.rs::execute_death_pipeline`.
   - Insurance state is split across three stores (`combat_wrecks_killmails.rs:29-235`), deleted in three separate steps (`:318`, `:319`, `:322`), and credited in a fourth step (`:349`) with no idempotency marker on the destroyed ship item. A failure/panic mid-sequence loses the insurance payout or leaves partial kill state.
2. **`with_mut_combat_runtime` under the DB writer wipes in-memory mutations (`EP-12`):**
   - When called while the current thread already holds `WorldRepository::writer` (`is_write_locked_by_current_thread`), `with_mut_combat_runtime` (`services/combat_crimewatch.rs:944-981`, `:509-522`) mutates memory only and sets `synced_db_epoch = 0`; the very next read sees `epoch == 0` and overwrites memory from the older persisted snapshot (dropping bounty pool / payout / insurance mutations, or leaving memory un-rolled-back if the outer tx aborts).
3. **Recursive `60 -> 60 combat_ephemeral` lock masked by `lock_rank_ratchet.txt:47-48` (`NEW-05`):**
   - `lock_rank.rs` keys rank-`60` checks by rank number rather than lock instance address, allowing `crates/eve-db/lock_rank_ratchet.txt:47-48` (`combat_crimewatch.rs::{sync_combat_runtime_from_db, with_combat_runtime}::combat_ephemeral`) to mask recursive acquisitions on the same `RwLock` (writer-starved recursive `.read()` deadlock, or `.read() -> .write()` self-deadlock at `:875` when `combat_state_epoch` advances).

## Required behaviour & acceptance tests
1. Route all weapon-RPC ship/capsule kills through `execute_death_pipeline`, consolidate insurance contracts onto `WorldStateSnapshot` only, and record insurance payout atomically inside the death transaction with an idempotency check.
2. Pass `&mut WorldStateSnapshot` explicitly into combat/bounty helpers called inside transactions instead of branching on `is_write_locked_by_current_thread` and setting `synced_db_epoch = 0`; assert a mutation inside `with_mut_snapshot` survives subsequent reads and rolls back cleanly on tx abort.
3. Refactor the recursive `with_combat_runtime` call chain so `lock_rank_ratchet.txt:47-48` are removed, and track `(rank, lock_addr)` in `crates/eve-db/src/lock_rank.rs` so same-lock recursion at rank `60` fails immediately in tests without adding false positives for distinct ordered rank-60 leaves.

Formally specify safety and governance invariants; test delegation, quorum, revocation, appeal, emergency suspension and conflicting rules. References: Zoo emergency-governance paper, Open Policy Agent.

Acceptance: machine-checked invariants and an adversarial rule-conflict test suite.

Part of the Zoo x Hanzo open research program (see the tracking issue in zoo-apps/papers). Every bounty produces BOTH an implementation and a research artifact: source code, a reproducible benchmark, a versioned specification or paper, and a clear statement of what remains unproven. Scientific claims need independently checkable evidence; governance decisions need authorized decision-makers; AI agents may recommend, flag conflicts, estimate value and prepare plans but must not redefine voting rules, authorize treasury spending or declare their own experiments valid. Production-bound source contributions are Apache-2.0; datasets, reasoning traces, model weights and external SDKs need a separate license review before use. Open for community research: comment to claim, publish method and raw numbers (bounty; reward terms are set by the maintainers on the issue). Zoo's published research describes these protocols; implementation status and production validation are to be confirmed per bounty.

raw.title: [Discussion]: AI usage policy
raw.body:
We've been kind of putting this topic off for a while now, because of how controversial of a topic it is, but I think we're very quickly reaching the point where we have to have some sort of policy governing our stance on AI usage in this project. This is because we've been getting more and more interactions from either autonomous agents or users using LLM-based tools in some capacity, and we are basically the only project left in the scene without SOME sort of AI policy.

We have just gotten someone, who either seems to be an agent themselves or at least is using an LLM, trying to implement a large feature (more on that below), which is what is spurring this discussion.

Because I know opinions on AI usage vary wildly from person to person, and some people have more nuanced opinions whereas some are strictly against, I'm opening this discussion issue to at least *try* and form some sort of official policy. @ashquarky made some blog posts about AI coding, specifically in homebrew, and I think it's a great "first read" for the topic https://heyquark.com/brew/2026/02/27/on-ai-homebrew/.

Some examples of AI contributions/interactions we've been getting:

- https://github.com/PretendoNetwork/juxtaposition/pull/431
- https://github.com/PretendoNetwork/splatoon/pull/19#issuecomment-4739818703
- https://github.com/PretendoNetwork/juxtaposition/issues/411#issuecomment-4031398593
- https://forum.pretendo.network/t/am-i-allowed-to-upload-network-code-for-a-wii-u-game-that-has-nex-servers-but-no-one-did-a-network-dump-for-them/29047
- https://github.com/PretendoNetwork/nex-protocols-common-go/pull/58 (this one is only suspected, not confirmed, based on some suspicious language/comment patterns and such, but even if there is an LLM used here it's not clear if it was used for code or just translations as the OP does not seem to be a native English speaker)
- https://github.com/PretendoNetwork/account/issues/202#issuecomment-5341573247 (this one is also only suspected, but very likely so, given the em-dash usage and some of the awkward writing like how the comment awkwardly self-references the issue it's being commented on)

Those last 2 are the 2 big motivators for me to make this issue so we can finally get a policy made, for 2 different reasons:

1. That last link is someone using an LLM who seemingly wants to contribute large scale features, some of which even touch things like user data and auth and such. This is fundamentally different in my opinion than other "smaller" uses some people may have, like automation or small bug fixes, and should be treated much more harshly imo. Having someone try to PR in potentially entire, large, features into the project is obviously not great, not only because reviewing large LLM PRs like that is annoying, but also for optics reasons because it would also basically immediately give us an AI-slop reputation
2. The second to last link touches game servers, which poses a genuine legal concern for us which I will touch on later when I give my own opinions

I'm sure there are other examples, this has been happening for a while now, those are just the ones I could quickly find in a couple minutes.

I will say though, no matter what a policy ends up looking like, the 1 thing I will die on is I cannot, in good conscience, greenlight any AI policy that allows LLMs to be used for game servers, even if it's more lenient in other places like the Discord bots or websites and such. We have to be EXTREMELY careful with how we implement things, any wrong move could get us nuked by Nintendo and so we take aggressive action against those trying to use things like console SDKs to contribute. Since the SDKs for these consoles have been leaked for years, and LLMs are trained on any data they can get their hands on with no regard to copyright or legality, they are ABSOLUTELY trained on leaked SDK docs/C headers/etc. This is especially a problem after the gigaleak happened a few years ago, where several Nintendo games (including those who used NEX) had their entire source code leaked, which means LLMs could very well not only be trained on SDK headers/docs, but ***entire leaked source code*** (especially ones that train off data from GitHub, since I know for a fact that at least one game from the gigaleak is still to this day available on GitHub, and it happens to be a 3DS game that uses NEX which a direct concern for us). So we can't trust any LLM to touch anything relating to game servers, as we have no way of knowing where the information it got is coming from and I'm simply not going to take that risk. This also very likely applies to things like https://github.com/PretendoNetwork/account/issues/202#issuecomment-5341573247, since even though I doubt the details of how NNAS worked have been leaked, I'm sure that parts of the leaked SDKs included how games would interact with the account server for service tokens and such, which is directly relevant in this case. I am also very strongly against the idea of letting LLMs make large features or features that deal with sensitive topics such as authentication/security/user data, whether or not a human is involved or not, such as https://github.com/PretendoNetwork/account/issues/202#issuecomment-5341573247

Some example policies from others in the scene:

- https://github.com/cemu-project/Cemu#ai-generated-contributions
- https://github.com/azahar-emu/azahar/blob/master/AI-POLICY.md
- https://github.com/dolphin-emu/dolphin/blob/46e38d28fa050ba1b9e933b57e1700a9073ce8ce/Contributing.md#generative-ai (this one also mentions the same legal concerns I have for the game servers)

raw.body:
@claude

# JoshyMC Lifesteal — Controlled Beta Testing Utilities

PRIORITY: P2
TYPE: TARGETED IMPLEMENTATION
SCOPE: Lifesteal only

## OBJECTIVE

Make controlled beta testing easier for staff without modifying live player progress unnecessarily.

Reuse existing Lifesteal administrative commands whenever possible.

Do not implement a new testing framework or duplicate existing staff tools.

## 1. EXISTING TOOLS

Review existing staff capabilities for:

- Setting test heart balances
- Issuing Heart items
- Managing ranked test matches
- Viewing player recovery status
- Managing Lifesteal teams
- Viewing bank and bounty diagnostics
- Checking progression state
- Viewing server health

Prefer documenting existing commands over creating new ones.

## 2. IDENTIFY ACTUAL GAPS

If a required beta scenario cannot be tested with existing safe commands, identify the smallest missing capability.

Examples:

- Preparing players for a ranked test match
- Checking whether a player has a pending restoration
- Resetting disposable testing conditions without affecting other players
- Confirming the active Lifesteal configuration

Do not automatically add new commands for every example.

## 3. SAFETY REQUIREMENTS

Any new test utility must:

- Require an explicit administrative permission.
- Be unavailable to regular players.
- Respect existing inventory and heart protections.
- Avoid running during unsafe ranked restoration states.
- Record state-changing operations in the existing audit log.
- Avoid creating duplicate currency, items or heart rewards.
- Never silently erase real player progress.

Prefer dedicated staging environments for destructive tests.

## 4. VALIDATION

Run applicable admin, ranked, heart, recovery and permission checks.

Run ./gradlew build if implementation changes are made.

## 5. DELIVERABLE

If existing staff commands are sufficient, publish a concise beta staff command reference and create no PR.

If a genuinely necessary testing capability is missing, implement only that capability in one focused PR.

Do not add unrelated features.

raw.body:
**Umbrella HIP**: [HIP-1348: Reliable, Economical and Verifiable AI Infrastructure](https://hips.hanzo.ai/docs/hip-1348-reliable-economical-and-verifiable-ai-infrastructure/) (`hanzoai/hips`)
**Bounty Class**: Research + Implementation Bounty
**Primary Research / Code**: [SLSA v1.2](https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.2/tracks) · [Sigstore Cosign](https://github.com/sigstore/cosign)

### Objective & Acceptance Test
Sign and verify build provenance (`source_revision`, toolchain, runtime digest, and output artifact digest) for agent-produced deliverables across `cloud` and `hanzoai/forge` (`issues` disabled on `forge`). Test tampering and unauthorized substitution rejection.

### Scope & Canonical Architecture
Tracked in `hanzoai/cloud` because `hanzoai/forge` has GitHub issues disabled.

Canonical stack boundaries MUST stay intact (`vfs -> hanzoai/s3 -> visor`, Cloud owning lifecycle & billing, Enso routing models, Zen generating outputs, Kai returning structured non-generative decisions). Reported figures in referenced FAST/conference papers belong strictly to the original authors' environments and MUST NOT be treated as Hanzo expectations until reproduced here.

### Research-to-PR Acceptance Contract (0 of 6 requirements)
- [ ] **1. Paper & License Audit**: Link primary paper/code, summarize design, and verify license compatibility (prefer Apache-2.0/MIT for production merges; clean-room implementation or research-only report otherwise) and patent restrictions.
- [ ] **2. Matched Baselines**: Provide reproducible upstream baseline and identical Hanzo baseline scripts/configs.
- [ ] **3. Falsifiable Hypothesis**: Document target metrics and expected failure modes up front.
- [ ] **4. Deliverable**: Submit bounded implementation PR (Implementation Bounty) or documented reproducible experiment including valid negative results (Research Bounty).
- [ ] **5. Evidence & Safety**: Include correctness, concurrency, multi-tenant isolation, security, and regression tests appropriate to the subsystem.
- [ ] **6. Measurements & HIP Update**: Publish raw before/after measurements, methodology, and status update against HIP-1348.

raw.title: 🔐 Toyol Pocket — Tindakan pemilik sebelum bayaran sebenar
raw.body:
# Toyol — Aktivasi laluan duit tanpa modal pemilik

**Status pemilik disahkan pada 10 November 2026:** TNG eKYC telah disahkan pengguna dan nombor akaun DuitNow tersedia (pindahan ujian belum dibuat). Identiti Taskmarket Base Mainnet telah didaftarkan; semakan `whoami` dan `wallet balance` berjaya, baki 0 USDC. Keystore kekal dalam Termux dengan mod 0600. Sandaran yang disulitkan telah lulus perbandingan SHA256 dan disalin ke folder Download pada telefon yang sama. Sandaran luar peranti belum selesai; kata laluan sandaran perlu diganti sebelum menyimpan nilai sebenar. Tiada rahsia disimpan dalam isu ini. 0 kerja berbayar diterima, RM0 disahkan masuk ke TNG, 0 USDC diterima.

## STATUS AKTIVASI DAN GERBANG BAKI

1. **TNG — SELESAI (persediaan sahaja):** TNG eWallet telah diverifikasi (eKYC) dan boleh menerima DuitNow. Nombor akaun DuitNow TNG hanya dimasukkan pada pembekal pembayaran rasmi apabila pembayaran MYR benar-benar wujud. **Jangan letak nombor itu dalam issue ini atau chat.** Panduan rasmi https://www.tngdigital.com.my/get-started/transfer/duitnow/
2. **Dompet ejen — SELESAI (persediaan sahaja):** Untuk menyertai bounty Taskmarket yang membayar USDC, identiti ejen/dompet pada **Base Mainnet** mesti diwujudkan secara selamat oleh pengendali di peranti dipercayai, selepas membaca syarat penggunaan. Panduan rasmi https://docs.taskmarket.dev/getting-started/install dan https://docs.taskmarket.dev/getting-started/first-task-worker. Pendaftaran melalui `taskmarket --network base init` percuma dan kebanyakan kerja tidak memerlukan deposit. **Jangan fund dompet, beli token, bayar yuran atau copy seed/private key ke chat/repo/issue.** Pengendali perlu simpan `~/.taskmarket/keystore.json` di tempat selamat, bukan repositori awam.
3. **Autonomi sebenar — BELUM AKTIF:** GitHub Actions yang kita gunakan tidak mempunyai akses ke dompet peribadi. Untuk penyerahan terus secara automatik, pengendali perlu membenarkan laluan tandatangan yang selamat. Pada masa ini tiada akses sebegitu, jadi Toyol **belum boleh claim/submit** ke marketplace dari CI. Jangan memintas kelulusan akaun atau keselamatan.
4. **Tunai keluar daripada USDC:** JANGAN masukkan token ke nombor TNG atau andaikan setiap bursa menyokong USDC di rangkaian Base. Semak bursa tersenarai di https://www.sc.com.my/regulation/guidelines/recognizedmarkets/list-of-registered-digital-asset-exchanges dan tanya bursa tersebut sama ada menerima tepat token, network, KYC, fi, had minimum dan pengeluaran bank. Jika sesuai, pindahan MYR daripada bank tempatan ke TNG melalui DuitNow boleh dibuat dengan pengesahan penerima.

## Polisi poket Toyol

- Belum menang: **REWARD LISTED — NOT OWNED**. Bukan wang.
- Kerja diterima tapi belum dibayar: **RECEIVABLE, NOT CASH**.
- USDC dibayar di dompet yang dimiliki dan disahkan: **ASSET OUTSIDE TNG**. Jangan gandakan sebagai RM.
- MYR dibayar di akaun penerima dan boleh dipindah melalui DuitNow: **CASHOUT READY**.
- TNG benar-benar dikreditkan, bukti diterima: **TNG RECEIVED**.

Poket bukan ewallet berfungsi dalam repo. Sistem kod hanya merekod bukti; tiada transaksi automatik tanpa identiti sah, arahan yang diizinkan dan akaun yang wujud.

**Penting:** Taskmarket hosted agents mungkin memerlukan kredit komputasi dan kelulusan akses. Itu bukan pilihan automatik buat masa ini kerana pemilik melarang penggunaan duit peribadi. https://docs.taskmarket.dev/hosted-agents/overview

## Operasi automatik sedia ada

Toyol Paid Tasks mencari peluang setiap 6 jam di https://github.com/ilhamraduanbis-source/toyol-digital/issues/4. Untuk menerima notifikasi isu GitHub, pemilik boleh klik **Subscribe** di issue #4 dan #5. Langganan GitHub itu tidak sama dengan notifikasi ChatGPT.

Tiada tawaran wang orang lain boleh dituntut tanpa memenuhi syarat kerja yang sah.


## Langkah teknikal selepas aktivasi

- Radar Taskmarket menolak kerja yang memerlukan pembelian seperti Lumen House. Penapis `REQUIRES_PURCHASE_OR_OUTLAY` dan ujian regresi ditambah pada 10 November 2026; workflow ujian GitHub Actions berjaya.
- GitHub Actions tidak memiliki keystore atau token peranti dan tidak berhak menandatangani serahan bagi pihak pemilik.
- Langkah seterusnya ialah mencari satu tugasan zero-cost yang benar-benar dalam keupayaan Toyol, menghasilkan bukti kerja, dan menyediakan mekanisme serahan bertandatangan terkawal. Jangan mensyaratkan pemilik membuka Termux untuk radar berjalan.


## Operasi cari pendapatan — 10 November 2026 (12:56 MYT)

- Radar manual melalui perubahan kod dijalankan dan selesai dengan kejayaan: https://github.com/ilhamraduanbis-source/toyol-digital/actions/runs/42758933427 . Ini **push run**, bukan bukti cron enam jam telah berlaku.
- Sumber dibaca: Jobbi 639 rekod; Taskmarket 3; BasedAgents 17. Sumber GitHub asal diperiksa untuk 14 calon dalam senarai akhir. Isu berstatus tutup tidak layak; isu yang ramai komen atau sudah ditugaskan ditanda sebagai risiko, bukan ditolak automatik kerana persaingan semata-mata.
- Taskmarket Lumen House memerlukan pembelian barang/NFT, ditolak menurut dasar modal RM0. Tugasan Tempo dengan token bukan USDC Base kini ditolak. Isu Algora yang sudah ada PR/assignment/aktiviti lama tidak dianggap terus sedia dibayar.
- Ujian terkini: **169/169 lulus**, 0 gagal: https://github.com/ilhamraduanbis-source/toyol-digital/actions/runs/42758933309 .
- **Bukti pendapatan:** 0 tuntutan baharu, 0 kerja diterima, 0 USDC diterima, RM0 diterima. Senarai iklan bukan earnings.
- **Gerbang yang masih terbuka:** tugas yang benar-benar boleh diselesaikan, izin penghantaran, tandatangan selamat, penerimaan pembeli, settlement dan off-ramp Malaysia.
- Tiada deposit, transaksi on-chain, atau secret pengguna dimuat naik.


## First income quest — semakan 10 November 2026

Arahan pemilik: terus cari pendapatan sebenar yang diperoleh oleh ejen, bukan peluang pekerjaan untuk pemilik. Operasi kekal modal RM0.

- Taskmarket Base: Lumen House 15 USDC memerlukan pembelian produk dan NFT, ditolak. Cine 2.5 USDC sudah tamat dan mempunyai 104 penghantaran.
- BasedAgents: semakan bebas melaporkan escrow null dan status pembayaran pending pada tawaran terbuka. Radar Toyol kini menolak tawaran tanpa bukti escrow daripada senarai boleh dicuba.
- GitHub: bounty $50 changelog mempunyai sekitar 2434 komen, Hanzo #8 hanya membayar mata reputasi, agentswarm-examples #14 hanya kredit laman tanpa pengeluaran, PotPie #224 sudah ditutup dan Highlight #8032 mempunyai berpuluh tuntutan belum dibayar.
- Penapisan terkini berjaya: 170/170 ujian (https://github.com/ilhamraduanbis-source/toyol-digital/actions/runs/42760735397), radar (https://github.com/ilhamraduanbis-source/toyol-digital/actions/runs/42760735380). Kedua-duanya ialah push runs, bukan bukti cron berjalan.
- Status audit semasa: 0 serahan sebenar, 0 penerimaan, 0 USDC diterima, RM0 disahkan.
- GitHub Actions radar setiap enam jam kekal dijadualkan. Tiada dompet/keystore/token/kata laluan dipindahkan ke GitHub. Pemilik tidak perlu membuka Termux untuk carian.
- Keutamaan seterusnya ialah satu tugasan baharu yang escrow terbukti, tiada modal, kemampuan diuji, izin penyerahan, dan laluan tandatangan sah. Jangan mereka-reka pendapatan atau berkongsi kunci.

## Percubaan kerja luar pertama — SwarmMemo (10 November 2026)

- Bukan ujian dalaman: implementasi kerja pihak ketiga SwarmMemo QA respons API dengan dua kes, bukti status/saiz/hash, deklarasi sebelum panggilan, laporan dan penyerahan bertandatangan. Upah 0.10 USDC di Base, kos penyertaan sifar.
- Tugasan langsung https://swarmmemo.com/work/481fbfae3a58712dfef55751aa81f209 . Requester mempunyai sejarah pembayaran 0.10 USDC yang direkod bersama hash transaksi di Base, tetapi payout khusus Toyol belum dijamin.
- Dua slot 10 November 2026 sudah penuh (claimable=false). Pembukaan berikutnya 11 November 2026 00:00 UTC (08:00 MYT).
- Workflow GitHub untuk cuba serah sekali sahaja: https://github.com/ilhamraduanbis-source/toyol-digital/actions/workflows/toyol-first-paid-qa.yml . Cron 23:56 UTC pra-pemanasan, tandatangan hanya jika slot terbuka serta syarat disahkan. Tidak menghantar ketika slot ditutup.
- Penerima ialah alamat awam Base Toyol. Private key Taskmarket kekal dalam Termux. Tandatangan SwarmMemo menggunakan identiti Ed25519 sementara dalam runner, tidak dipaparkan/disimpan dalam GitHub.
- Run read-only semasa https://github.com/ilhamraduanbis-source/toyol-digital/actions/runs/42762571326 mengesahkan tiada slot sekarang.
- Status terkini: kerja luar belum dituntut/diserah, penerimaan 0, USDC diterima 0. Workflow siap tidak sama dengan pendapatan.


## First Income Quest — operasi 11 November 2026

Arahan pengasas: Toyol perlu mencari kerja luar, belajar menyesuaikan penyelesaian kepada tugasan sebenar, menyerahkan hasil dan membawa balik pendapatan. Lulus ujian dalaman bukan sasaran.

- **Pasaran yang turut disemak:** SwarmMemo 0.02/0.10 USDC data/QA, voiceio direktori 1 USDC, voiceio AUR/nixpkgs 3 USDC, GitHub developer bounties; tugas yang memerlukan pembelian, modal, stake, penyenaraian palsu, spam, atau pembayaran kredit tidak boleh tunai ditolak.
- **Cubaan QA 0.10 USDC:** jadual dijalankan lebih awal mulai 23:30 UTC dan menunggu pelepasan slot 00:00 UTC; klien SwarmMemo dipautkan kepada commit dan Git blob tetap. Script: src/swarmmemo-first-paid-qa.py; workflow: .github/workflows/toyol-first-paid-qa.yml.
- **Kerja luar kedua 0.02 USDC:** pelaksana mengambil data NOAA dari alat awam, mengesahkan SHA-256, mencap bukti notary, menghasilkan ringkasan berfakta, menyiarkan di #research dan menghantar kepada tugasan melalui tandatangan identiti agen terasing. Hanya menuntut jika slot tersedia. Script: src/swarmmemo-paid-data-brief.py; workflow: .github/workflows/toyol-paid-data-brief.yml.
- **Bukti pembayaran:** pemantau membaca keputusan asal SwarmMemo dan hanya memberitahu pemilik melalui komen pada isu ini apabila ada USDC berstatus paid kepada alamat awam Base Toyol berserta tx hash. Script: src/swarmmemo-payout-observer.py; workflow: .github/workflows/toyol-usdc-receipt-watch.yml. Run 42932388441 berjaya melakukan semakan dan mendapati tiada pembayaran.
- **Pencapaian hari ini:** dua pelaksana tugas luar, dan satu pemantau bayaran; semakan read-only pada 08:31 MYT mendapati slot data brief telah penuh. Kedua-dua penghantaran berjadual masih belum berlaku dan tidak boleh dianggap berfungsi sepenuhnya sehingga log sebenar wujud.
- **Status wang:** 0 USDC disahkan diterima oleh Toyol, RM0 di TNG disahkan. Tiada deposit, modal, transaksi dompet atau keystore di GitHub. Kejayaan selepas ini mesti diukur sebagai hasil diterima dan USDC masuk, kemudian pengeluaran MYR berasingan.

## Acceptance crit

raw.title: Curate published bug bounties and source references for Opportunities
raw.body:
## Goal
Curate a truthful Opportunities directory with published Ethereum and Solana bug bounty programs, public source references, and the separate runnable VeriPoC vault fixture.

## Acceptance criteria
- List eight externally hosted bug bounties from current official Immunefi pages, with Ethereum and/or Solana badges, published maximum rewards, and a dated source check.
- Provide an internal detail page for each bounty with concise instruction and scope summaries, links to the official rules and scope, and public audits or known issues where verified.
- Use one accessible category filter row plus search. Show all entries by default; keep source and practice references available.
- Direct external bounty submissions to the official host. External cards cannot trigger VeriPoC verification or report submission.
- Keep ten read-only pinned public source references and the reviewed Demo Vault as the sole runnable local fixture.
- Test category/search navigation, responsive widths, official links, and negative authorization boundaries; run web build, typecheck, lint, browser and existing verification checks as appropriate.
- Preserve the published Agent Card and backend behavior.

## Boundaries
A published bounty is not permission for VeriPoC to run arbitrary contracts or agent-generated PoCs. The official program rules govern testing, eligibility and disclosure. The directory is a dated static snapshot, not a live status feed. No new backend endpoints, uploads, or external worker execution.

## Dependency
This directory revision stays within #42 / PR #44. General external-target execution remains separate future work.

raw.title: [Bounty proposal] Fix ttnn.rotate crashes, device hangs, and CB misbinding across sharded/interleaved memory_config transitions
raw.body:
### Summary

`ttnn.rotate` accepts an explicit output `memory_config` parameter (`ttnn.rotate(input_tensor, angle, ..., memory_config=...)`), and `RotateDeviceOperation::compute_output_specs` supports creating either sharded or interleaved output tensors independently of the input tensor's memory configuration.

However, both `NearestProgramFactory` and `BilinearProgramFactory` conflate input sharding with output sharding (`any_sharded`), resulting in multiple deterministic host crashes (`std::bad_optional_access`, `TT_FATAL`), L1 circular buffer aliasing bugs, and a device hang when `input_tensor.memory_config()` and the requested output `memory_config` differ or when an output shard grid has surplus cores.

---

### Root Cause Analysis (Verified on `main` @ `0de8c7f3aade6170fc456b904dbf72e3f776b6aa`)

#### 1. `NearestProgramFactory::create_descriptor` crashes with `std::bad_optional_access` and misbinds `output_cb` when input is `HEIGHT_SHARDED` and output is `INTERLEAVED` (`DRAM` or `L1`)
- In [`ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/pool/rotate/device/rotate_nearest_program_factory.cpp#L94-L100`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/0de8c7f3aade6170fc456b904dbf72e3f776b6aa/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/pool/rotate/device/rotate_nearest_program_factory.cpp#L94-L100):
  ```cpp
  if (is_sharded && !is_nd_sharded) {
      const auto input_shard_spec = input_tensor.shard_spec().value();
      all_cores = input_shard_spec.grid;
      num_cores = input_shard_spec.num_cores();
      input_nsticks_per_core = input_shard_spec.shape[0];
      output_nsticks_per_core = output_tensor.shard_spec().value().shape[0];
  ```
  `is_sharded` only checks `input_tensor.is_sharded()`. When `output_tensor` is `DRAM_MEMORY_CONFIG` or `L1_MEMORY_CONFIG` (interleaved), `output_tensor.shard_spec()` is `std::nullopt`, throwing `std::bad_optional_access`.
- In [`rotate_nearest_program_factory.cpp#L134-L135`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/0de8c7f3aade6170fc456b904dbf72e3f776b6aa/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/pool/rotate/device/rotate_nearest_program_factory.cpp#L134-L135):
  `aligned_output_stick_nbytes` checks `any_sharded` (which is derived solely from `input_tensor`) instead of checking whether `output_tensor` is sharded, using an unaligned stick size when writing from a sharded input to a DRAM-interleaved output (or vice versa).
- In [`rotate_nearest_program_factory.cpp#L184-L196`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/0de8c7f3aade6170fc456b904dbf72e3f776b6aa/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/pool/rotate/device/rotate_nearest_program_factory.cpp#L184-L196):
  `output_cb` is only a burst staging FIFO between `reader_rotate_nearest_interleaved.cpp` and `writer_rotate_nearest_interleaved.cpp` (which always writes every output stick via `TensorAccessor` `output_tensor_accessor`). Binding `.buffer = any_sharded ? output_tensor.buffer() : nullptr` fails with `TT_FATAL: Only L1 buffers can have an associated circular buffer!` when `output_tensor` is in DRAM, corrupts L1 when `output_tensor` is L1 interleaved, and causes race conditions when `input_tensor` and `output_tensor` have different `HEIGHT_SHARDED` shard specs.

#### 2. `BilinearProgramFactory::create_descriptor` fails when input is `HEIGHT_SHARDED` and output is `INTERLEAVED` (or uses a different `HEIGHT_SHARDED` spec)
- In [`ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/pool/rotate/device/rotate_bilinear_program_factory.cpp#L136`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/0de8c7f3aade6170fc456b904dbf72e3f776b6aa/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/pool/rotate/device/rotate_bilinear_program_factory.cpp#L136), `const bool any_sharded = is_input_sharded || is_output_sharded;` is used to configure `output_cb` ([L201-L215](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/0de8c7f3aade6170fc456b904dbf72e3f776b6aa/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/pool/rotate/device/rotate_bilinear_program_factory.cpp#L201-L215)) and to skip creating `writer_desc` ([L318](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/0de8c7f3aade6170fc456b904dbf72e3f776b6aa/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/pool/rotate/device/rotate_bilinear_program_factory.cpp#L318), [L377](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/0de8c7f3aade6170fc456b904dbf72e3f776b6aa/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/pool/rotate/device/rotate_bilinear_program_factory.cpp#L377)).
- When `is_input_sharded && !is_output_sharded`:
  - `output_cb` is bound to `output_tensor.buffer()` (throwing `TT_FATAL: Only L1 buffers can have an associated circular buffer!` for DRAM output, or aliasing the interleaved L1 buffer across cores), and `writer_grid_sample_interleaved.cpp` is never launched to drain `output_cb`.
- Furthermore, `reader_rotate_bilinear_interleaved.cpp` reads from `input_tensor` exclusively via `TensorAccessor` (`input_tensor_accessor`) into an unbacked local `input_cb`. Only `output_cb` is backed by a tensor buffer when `is_output_sharded` is true. Partitioning cores by `output_shard_spec` when `is_output_sharded` is true and by `split_work_to_cores` when `is_output_sharded` is false allows `BilinearProgramFactory` to handle any combination of `HEIGHT_SHARDED` and `INTERLEAVED` inputs/outputs (including uneven shards and distinct input/output shard specs).

#### 3. `BilinearProgramFactory::create_descriptor` hangs the device when `output_shard_spec.grid` has more cores than active stick shards
- In [`rotate_bilinear_program_factory.cpp#L114-L123`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/0de8c7f3aade6170fc456b904dbf72e3f776b6aa/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/pool/rotate/device/rotate_bilinear_program_factory.cpp#L114-L123):
  ```cpp
  } else if (is_output_sharded) {
      const auto output_shard_spec = output_tensor.shard_spec().value();
      output_nsticks_per_core = output_shard_spec.shape[0];
      num_cores = (total_output_sticks + output_nsticks_per_core - 1) / output_nsticks_per_core;
      all_cores = output_shard_spec.grid;
  ```
  Both `reader_desc` and `compute_desc_group_1` (`total_interpolations = output_nsticks_per_core`) are launched on `all_cores` (`output_shard_spec.grid`), but runtime arguments are only populated for `num_cores`. If `output_shard_spec.grid.num_cores() > num_cores` (e.g. 100 sticks with `shard_height = 36` on a 4-core grid), the remaining core(s) receive default `num_sticks = 0` in the reader while `compute_pool_2d` blocks indefinitely waiting for `output_nsticks_per_core` pages. Setting `num_cores = output_shard_spec.num_cores()` matches the `is_input_sharded` path, allowing `reader_rotate_bilinear_interleaved.cpp` to push fill pages for `curr_batch >= input_batch`.

#### 4. Missing output `memory_config` validation in `RotateDeviceOperation::validate_inputs`
- [`rotate_device_operation.cpp#L60-L66`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/0de8c7f3aade6170fc456b904dbf72e3f776b6aa/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/pool/rotate/device/rotate_device_operation.cpp#L60-L66) validates `input.memory_config()`, but never validates `operation_attributes.memory_config` (allowing `WIDTH_SHARDED`/`BLOCK_SHARDED` output configs, mismatched shard widths, or `ND_SHARDED` configs in bilinear mode to reach the program factories and crash).

---

### Minimal Reproducer

```python
import torch
import ttnn

def test_repro(device):
    torch_input = torch.randn((1, 8, 8, 64), dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    shard_spec = ttnn.ShardSpec(
        ttnn.CoreRangeSet({ttnn.CoreRange(ttnn.CoreCoord(0, 0), ttnn.CoreCoord(1, 0))}),
        (32, 64),
        ttnn.ShardOrientation.ROW_MAJOR,
    )
    sharded_cfg = ttnn.MemoryConfig(ttnn.TensorMemoryLayout.HEIGHT_SHARDED, ttnn.BufferType.L1, shard_spec)

    ttnn_in_sharded = ttnn.from_torch(
        torch_input, layout=ttnn.ROW_MAJOR_LAYOUT, device=device, memory_config=sharded_cfg
    )

    # 1. Nearest: HEIGHT_SHARDED input -> DRAM_MEMORY_CONFIG output
    # Crashes on main with: std::bad_optional_access at rotate_nearest_program_factory.cpp:99
    out_nearest = ttnn.rotate(
        ttnn_in_sharded, angle=45.0, interpolation_mode="nearest", memory_config=ttnn.DRAM_MEMORY_CONFIG
    )

    # 2. Bilinear: HEIGHT_SHARDED input -> DRAM_MEMORY_CONFIG output
    # Crashes on main with: TT_FATAL: Only L1 buffers can have an associated circular buffer!
    out_bilinear = ttnn.rotate(
        ttnn_in_sharded, angle=45.0, interpolation_mode="bilinear", memory_config=ttnn.DRAM_MEMORY_CONFIG
    )
```

---

### Proposed Fix

1. **`rotate_device_operation.cpp`**: Validate `operation_attributes.memory_config` (require `HEIGHT_SHARDED` in `L1` and matching channel shard width when sharded, and require legacy `ShardSpec` in `bilinear` mode).
2. **`rotate_nearest_program_factory.cpp`**: Decouple input sharding from output sharding when computing `aligned_output_stick_nbytes`, remove the unconditional `output_tensor.shard_spec().value()` dereference, and keep `output_cb` as a local double-buffered burst FIFO (`num_cb_pages * NEAREST_BUFFERING_FACTOR`, `.buffer = nullptr`).
3. **`rotate_bilinear_program_factory.cpp`**: Drive output CB backing and core partitioning by `is_output_sharded` (using `num_cores = output_shard_spec.num_cores()` to prevent hangs on surplus grid cores, and using `split_work_to_cores` + `writer_grid_sample_interleaved.cpp` whenever `!is_output_sharded`).
4. **`test_rotate.py`**: Add unit tests covering `HEIGHT_SHARDED <-> INTERLEAVED` (`DRAM`/`L1`), `HEIGHT_SHARDED -> HEIGHT_SHARDED` with distinct shard grids/heights, uneven sharding with surplus grid cores, and invalid output `memory_config` rejection.

raw.title: [Bounty proposal] Fix ttnn.grid_sample memory_config overrides, sharded/interleaved factories, and padding OOB reads
raw.body:
### Summary

`ttnn.grid_sample` (`ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/pool/grid_sample/`) currently contains three related memory-configuration and bounds-checking defects across `GridSampleOperation::compute_output_specs`, `GridSampleBilinearProgramFactory`, `GridSampleNearestProgramFactory`, and the dataflow kernels:

1. **Caller-provided `memory_config` is silently ignored when `grid` is `HEIGHT_SHARDED` (`grid_sample_device_operation.cpp:198-270, 331`)**:
   - In `ttnn::prim::grid_sample` (`grid_sample_device_operation.cpp:331`), `.output_mem_config` defaults to `memory_config.value_or(grid.memory_config())`, which carries `grid.shard_spec()` even when `memory_config` is omitted.
   - To avoid using `grid`'s coordinate shard width (`2*K` or `6*K`) as the output shard width (`C` or `C*K`), `compute_output_specs` guards both the `INTERLEAVED` bilinear branch (`line 200`) and the explicit `shard_spec().has_value()` branch (`line 206`) with `!grid_tensor.memory_config().is_sharded()`.
   - Consequently, whenever `grid_tensor` is `HEIGHT_SHARDED`:
     - Passing `memory_config=ttnn.DRAM_MEMORY_CONFIG` or `ttnn.L1_MEMORY_CONFIG` (`INTERLEAVED`) in `bilinear` mode is **silently ignored** and replaced with a `HEIGHT_SHARDED` L1 output on `grid_tensor`'s core grid.
     - Passing a custom `HEIGHT_SHARDED` `memory_config` with a different `ShardSpec` (core grid, orientation, or shard height) in either `nearest` or `bilinear` mode is **silently ignored** and replaced with `grid_tensor`'s `ShardSpec`.

2. **Program factories conflate `grid_tensor.is_sharded()` with `output_tensor.is_sharded()` (`grid_sample_bilinear_program_factory.cpp:33, 60-82, 202-216, 367-452` and `grid_sample_nearest_program_factory.cpp:29, 51-74`)**:
   - Both `GridSampleBilinearProgramFactory::create_descriptor` and `GridSampleNearestProgramFactory::create_descriptor` set `is_sharded = grid_tensor.is_sharded()` and assume `grid_tensor` and `output_tensor` always have identical sharding state, core grids, orientations, and corresponding shard heights.
   - In `GridSampleBilinearProgramFactory`:
     - When `grid_tensor` is `INTERLEAVED` and `output_tensor` is `HEIGHT_SHARDED`, `is_sharded` is `false`, so `output_cb` is left unbacked (`nullptr`), work is partitioned across the full device compute grid instead of `output_tensor.shard_spec().grid`, and `writer_grid_sample_interleaved.cpp` attempts interleaved page writes into a sharded L1 output buffer.
     - When `grid_tensor` is `HEIGHT_SHARDED` and `output_tensor` is `INTERLEAVED`, `output_tensor.shard_spec().value()` throws `std::bad_optional_access`.
   - In both factories, when `grid_tensor` and `output_tensor` are both `HEIGHT_SHARDED` with different `ShardSpec`s, aliasing `grid_cb` directly to `grid_tensor.buffer()` reads mismatched local L1 shards instead of reading `grid_tensor` pages via `TensorAccessor`.

3. **Out-of-bounds NoC reads on trailing shard padding sticks (`writer_grid_sample_nearest_sharded.cpp:227-235` and `reader_grid_sample_interleaved_start_id.cpp:29, 72-97`)**:
   - In `writer_grid_sample_nearest_sharded.cpp:227-235`, `if constexpr (!is_sharded) { noc.async_read(grid_tensor_accessor, ..., {.page_id = grid_stick_idx + start_page_id}, {}); }` executes **before** `if (curr_batch < batch_size)`. When an output shard has trailing padding sticks (`curr_batch >= batch_size`), it issues out-of-bounds NoC reads past the end of `grid_tensor` before discarding the read data in the `else` branch.
   - In `reader_grid_sample_interleaved_start_id.cpp:29, 72-97`, `ct_arg[5]` (`input_batch`) is passed by `GridSampleBilinearProgramFactory` (`:228`) but ignored by the kernel. When `output_tensor` is `HEIGHT_SHARDED` with uneven shards or surplus cores (`curr_batch >= input_batch`), `spatial_pos` reads past the end of `grid_tensor` instead of pushing zero-weight placeholder pages to `scalar_dfb` and `input_dfb`.

---

### Proposed Fix

1. **`grid_sample_device_operation.cpp`**:
   - In `ttnn::prim::grid_sample`, when `memory_config` is omitted, default `.output_mem_config` to `MemoryConfig(grid.memory_config().memory_layout(), grid.memory_config().buffer_type())` (with `shard_spec = std::nullopt`) so `output_mem_config.shard_spec().has_value()` is `true` if and only if the caller explicitly supplied a `ShardSpec`.
   - In `GridSampleOperation::compute_output_specs`, respect `INTERLEAVED` `output_mem_config` in `bilinear` mode and explicit `output_mem_config.shard_spec()` in both `nearest` and `bilinear` modes regardless of whether `grid_tensor` is sharded.
   - In `GridSampleOperation::validate_on_program_cache_miss`, validate explicit output `ShardSpec` buffer type (`L1`), height divisibility (`output_sticks_per_grid_stick`), and width (`C_padded`).
2. **`grid_sample_nearest_program_factory.cpp` & `grid_sample_bilinear_program_factory.cpp`**:
   - Gate the zero-copy local L1 `grid_cb` fast path (`is_sharded`) on `grid_tensor` and `output_tensor` both being sharded with matching `grid`, `orientation`, and corresponding `shape[0]`.
   - In `GridSampleBilinearProgramFactory`, separate `is_output_sharded = output_tensor.is_sharded()` from `is_sharded` so `HEIGHT_SHARDED <-> INTERLEAVED` and distinct `HEIGHT_SHARDED` `ShardSpec`s partition work and configure `output_cb` / `has_writer` / `enable_split_reader` accurately.
3. **`writer_grid_sample_nearest_sharded.cpp` & `reader_grid_sample_interleaved_start_id.cpp`**:
   - Move the `!is_sharded` `grid_tensor_accessor` NoC read inside `if (curr_batch < batch_size)` in `writer_grid_sample_nearest_sharded.cpp`.
   - Read `input_batch = get_compile_time_arg_val(5)` in `reader_grid_sample_interleaved_start_id.cpp` and guard `grid_tensor_accessor` reads with `if (curr_batch < input_batch)`, pushing zero-weight placeholder pages when `curr_batch >= input_batch`.
4. **`tests/ttnn/unit_tests/operations/pool/test_grid_sample.py`**:
   - Add unit test coverage for `HEIGHT_SHARDED` grid -> `INTERLEAVED` (`DRAM`/`L1`) output in `bilinear` mode, `INTERLEAVED` grid -> custom `HEIGHT_SHARDED` output with trailing shard padding sticks, and `HEIGHT_SHARDED` grid -> distinct `HEIGHT_SHARDED` `ShardSpec` output in both `nearest` and `bilinear` modes.

raw.title: [Bounty Proposal] Fix silent NaN index corruption, outer-padding OOB indices, preallocated output hazards, and Quasar build failure in ttnn.argmax NC & W%32==0 paths
raw.body:
### Background & Summary

`ttnn.argmax` dispatches two major classes of reductions into the register-based compute-kernel NC path (`ttnn::prim::argmax_nc`):
1. **All non-HW reductions** (`dim < rank - 2` on rank `>= 3`, for both `TILE` and `ROW_MAJOR` inputs via `should_use_nc_path` in `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/reduction/argmax/argmax.cpp:66-90`).
2. **All `ROW_MAJOR` height reductions (`dim == rank - 2`) whenever `W % 32 == 0`** (`should_split_w_for_nc` in `argmax.cpp:48-60, 274-296`, which reshapes `(..., H, W)` into `(..., H, W/32, 32)` so `H` becomes a non-HW axis).

Auditing `argmax.cpp`, `argmax_nc_device_operation.cpp`, `argmax_nc_program_factory.cpp`, and `device/kernels/argmax_nc_compute.cpp` uncovered **five compounding correctness, memory-safety, and architecture-portability defects** in these paths:

1. **Silent `NaN` index corruption & width-dependent parity split (`W = 31` vs `W = 32`)**: Every other `ttnn.argmax` path (`argmax_common.hpp`, `argmax_tile_layout.hpp`, `argmax_tile_h_col.hpp`, `reader_argmax_interleaved_multicore.cpp`) enforces `torch.argmax` semantics (`NaN` dominates all finite/`±inf` values; first `NaN` wins ties). `argmax_nc_compute.cpp:98` uses `gt_binary_tile` alone, whose FP32 SFPU implementation (`calculate_binary_comp_fp32_strict_ordered` in `ckernel_sfpu_binary_comp.h:106-107`) rejects `NaN` (`abs(a) + abs(b) <= inf`) and returns `0` whenever either operand is `NaN`. Because `test_argmax_nan_and_signed_zero_matches_torch` in `tests/ttnn/unit_tests/operations/reduce/test_argmax.py:581-586` parameterized `(ROW_MAJOR, -1)`, `(TILE, -1)`, and `(TILE, -2)` while omitting `(ROW_MAJOR, -2)` and non-HW dims, `[32, 64]` `ROW_MAJOR` `dim=-2` silently returns wrong indices (`2` instead of `1` on `["1.0", "+nan", "2.0"]`, `0` instead of `1` on `["-inf", "+nan"]`), breaking parity even between `W = 63` (`argmax_tile_h_col.hpp` -> `1`) and `W = 64` (`argmax_nc` -> `2`) on identical column data.
2. **Out-of-bounds indices & slab-stride corruption when outer dims carry padding**: `ArgMaxNCDeviceOperation::create_descriptor` (`argmax_nc_program_factory.cpp:57-63`) sets `num_reduce_tiles = input.padded_shape()[normalized_dim]` instead of `input.logical_shape()[normalized_dim]`. When `padded_shape[normalized_dim] > logical_shape[normalized_dim]` and logical values along `dim` are negative (e.g. log-probabilities `-2.0` with `0.0` padding), `argmax_nc` reduces across padded slices and emits **out-of-bounds indices `>= logical_shape[dim]`** (causing downstream `gather`/`embedding` OOB reads). Moreover, unreduced outer-dim padding mismatches `input.padded_shape()` slab strides against `compute_output_specs()`'s unpadded `output.logical_shape()`.
3. **Missing `optional_output_tensor` / `preallocated_output` validation & rank-compat crash (NOC OOB read/write risk)**:
   - `ArgMaxNCDeviceOperation::validate_on_program_cache_miss` (`argmax_nc_device_operation.cpp:48-58`) never checks `is_device_tensor`, `out.device() == input.device()`, `INTERLEAVED` memory layout, `sub_core_grids` device-grid containment, or **output shape/volume equality**. Because `create_descriptor` derives `num_output_tiles = output.physical_volume() / TILE_HW`, an oversized `preallocated_output` drives `reader_argmax_nc.cpp` to read past the end of `input_buffer` over NOC, while a sharded `preallocated_output` writes interleaved page IDs into sharded buffers.
   - `argmax.cpp:264-268, 291-294` calls `ttnn::copy(nc_result, optional_output_tensor.value())` without enforcing `ArgMaxDeviceOperation`'s contract (`dtype == UINT32`, `ROW_MAJOR`, `INTERLEAVED`, page-compatible shape). Passing a `BFLOAT16`/`FLOAT32` output silently typecasts instead of failing with `"Only UINT32 is supported for outputs"`, whereas passing a valid rank-differing page-compatible shared sampling buffer (e.g. rank-4 `[1, 2, 32, 64]` for `keepdim=False` result `[2, 32, 64]`, explicitly supported by `argmax_device_operation.cpp:155-165`) crashes inside `ttnn::copy`.
4. **Hard kernel compile / DFB validation failure on Quasar (`tt::ARCH::QUASAR`)**: While `ArgMaxDeviceOperation` (`argmax_device_operation.cpp:101-108`, `argmax_multi_core_program_factory.cpp:208-214`, `argmax_single_core_program_factory.cpp`) was ported to Quasar, `should_use_nc_path` and `should_split_w_for_nc` still route Quasar tensors into `argmax_nc`, which fails to build/validate on Quasar: `gt_binary_tile` / `gt_binary_tile_init` are compiled out under `#ifndef ARCH_QUASAR` (`eltwise_binary_sfpu.h:186, 224`), `DataFormat::UInt32` does not exist in Quasar's kernel `DataFormat` enum (`fill_tile_int<DataFormat::UInt32>` at `argmax_nc_compute.cpp:88, 105`) and is rejected by Quasar CB/DFB validation (`argmax_nc_program_factory.cpp:70`), and Quasar's `where_tile` (`ckernel_sfpu_where.h:31-38`) loads/stores operands as `sfpi::vFloat`.
5. **Sub-core-grid row/column split inconsistency & Wormhole B0 `HiFi4 + fp32_dest_acc_en` hazard**:
   - `argmax_nc_program_factory.cpp:95` calls `split_work_to_cores(*operation_attributes.sub_core_grids, num_output_tiles)` with default `row_wise = false` (column-wise `core_group_1`/`core_group_2`), whereas lines `199-204` enumerate `ordered_cores` row-wise (`for y .. for x`).
   - `run_argmax_nc` (`argmax.cpp:110-111`) hardcodes `MathFidelity::HiFi4` while `argmax_nc_program_factory.cpp:82` forces `fp32_dest_acc_en = true`, hitting the Wormhole B0 `HiFi4 + fp32_dest_acc_en` issue (`#38306`, avoided via `HiFi3` on Wormhole B0 in `reduce_op.cpp:144-152`).

---

### Root Cause Analysis (Exact File & Line References)

#### 1. `NaN` Ignored in `argmax_nc_compute.cpp` + Width-Dependent Dispatch in `argmax.cpp`
- In `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/reduction/argmax/device/kernels/argmax_nc_compute.cpp:98-108`:
  ```cpp
  gt_binary_tile(dst_scratch_a, dst_max, dst_scratch_b);
  where_tile<DataFormat::Float32>(dst_scratch_b, dst_scratch_a, dst_max, dst_max);
  fill_tile_int<DataFormat::UInt32>(dst_scratch_a, k);
  where_tile<DataFormat::Int32>(dst_scratch_b, dst_scratch_a, dst_argmax, dst_argmax);
  ```
- In `tt_metal/hw/ckernels/wormhole_b0/metal/llk_api/llk_sfpu/ckernel_sfpu_binary_comp.h:106-107`, `calculate_binary_comp_fp32_strict_ordered` executes:
  ```cpp
  // if abs(a) + abs(b) <= inf; rejects NaN
  TTI_SFPIADD(0, inf, sum, sfpi::SFPIADD_MOD1_ARG_2SCOMP_LREG_DST | sfpi::SFPIADD_MOD1_CC_GTE0);
  ```
  Whenever `new_val` at `k >= 1` is `+NaN` (`0x7fc00000`) or `-NaN` (`0xffc00000`), `gt_binary_tile` writes `0` to `dst_scratch_b`, so `NaN` never updates `dst_max` or `dst_argmax`.
- Because `should_split_w_for_nc` (`argmax.cpp:52-60`) triggers iff `input.layout() == ROW_MAJOR && normalized_dim == rank - 2 && width % 32 == 0`, reducing `shape = [32, 63]` along `dim = 0` takes `argmax_tile_h_col.hpp` (returning `1` for `[1.0, NaN, 2.0]`), whereas `shape = [32, 64]` takes `argmax_nc` (returning `2`).

#### 2. `num_reduce_tiles` Computed from `padded_shape` Instead of `logical_shape`
- In `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/reduction/argmax/device/argmax_nc_program_factory.cpp:57-63`:
  ```cpp
  const auto& input_shape = input.padded_shape();
  ...
  const auto [inner_tile_size, reduce_tile_size] = extract_nc_strides(input_shape, normalized_dim);
  const uint32_t num_reduce_tiles = input_shape[normalized_dim];
  ```
  `extract_nc_strides` rightly uses `padded_shape` for physical inter-slab strides, but `num_reduce_tiles` must be `input.logical_shape()[normalized_dim]` so `reader_argmax_nc.cpp` and `argmax_nc_compute.cpp` only consider valid logical indices `k in [0, logical_shape[normalized_dim])`.

#### 3. Preallocated Output Validation & Rank-Compatible Shared Buffers
- `argmax_nc_device_operation.cpp:48-58` only checks `out.dtype() == UINT32` and `out.layout() == TILE`.
- `argmax.cpp:264-268` and `291-294` skip `ArgMaxDeviceOperation`'s `optional_output_tensor` checks (`argmax_device_operation.cpp:141-165`) and fail when `nc_result.logical_shape()` and `optional_output_tensor->logical_shape()` have different ranks but identical volume and last-dim page width.

#### 4. Quasar Dispatch & Kernel Incompatibility
- `argmax.cpp:48-90` dispatches Quasar tensors into `run_argmax_nc` -> `ttnn::prim::argmax_nc` where `gt_binary_tile` is `#ifndef ARCH_QUASAR` and `DataFormat::UInt32` is unsupported on Quasar.

---

### Minimal Reproduction

#### 1. Python / `ttnn` Reproduction (Fails Today on Wormhole / Blackhole)
```python
import torch
import ttnn

def test_repro_argmax_nc_bugs(device):
    # 1) ROW_MAJOR dim=-2 width=63 (passes) vs width=64 (silently corrupted via should_split_w_for_nc -> argmax_nc)
    for w in (63, 64):
        t = torch.full((32, w), -10.0, dtype=torch.float32)
        t[0, :] = 1.0
        t[1, :] = float("nan")
        t[2, :] = 2.0
        tt_in = ttnn.from_torch(t, device=device, layout=ttnn.ROW_MAJOR_LAYOUT)
        got = ttnn.to_torch(ttnn.from_device(ttnn.argmax(tt_in, dim=-2))).to(torch.int64)
        ref = torch.argmax(t, dim=-2)
        assert torch.equal(got, ref), f"W={w}: expected {ref[0].item()}, got {got[0].item()}"
        # W=63 -> 1 (matches PyTorch); W=64 -> 2 (BUG: NaN ignored!)

    # 2) Non-HW NC reduction (dim=0 / dim=1) with NaN and +/-inf
```

## Gap-auditor findings to fix

3. **Daily Goals (`quasar_daily_goals.rs:198-274`):** Initializes `DailyGoalManager` with zero active templates in production unless admin-seeded in tests, and `build_sde_daily_goal_templates` uses synthetic rules; tagged admin tests only check `!notifs.is_empty()` rather than decoding concrete Quasar notice payloads.

2. **Seed production startup from `evomu_sde.sqlite`** so a fresh server starts with populated AIR Career goals, Achievement categories/definitions, and active daily goals without test-only admin calls. Where specific server-authoritative reward values do not exist anywhere in client files, follow `AGENTS.md:71` strictly (verify absence from `code.ccp`/`ResFiles`, label operator-configurable defaults honestly, and document any genuine external-server data boundary).
3. **Strengthen Quasar notice & admin tests** so every `notices_pb2.pyj` and `admin/*_pb2.pyj` test decodes and asserts exact protobuf fields (`CompletedNotice`, progress delta, reward entitlement, showcase update).

Clears `21` active `FLAGGED_FAKE` parity rows (and unblocks `plan:MN-02` + `plan:E-5`) identified in the latest `parity.json` / `auditor_rows.json` on `main` (`4d49958c4`). Touch `crates/`, `tools/sde-import/`, and `docs/parity/` ONLY (never edit `.agents/` or `AGENTS.md`).

## Problem

`final_gate.py:353` requires `open_rows == 0` and `flagged_fake == 0`. In Space, Mining, Equinox Sovereignty, and Missions, `21` rows are currently `FLAGGED_FAKE` because handlers rely on synthetic/derived constants instead of imported SDE / client FSD data or complete domain mechanics:

### 1. Mining & Navigation (`3` rows; unblocks `plan:MN-02`)
- `feat:mining.belts-as-balls` & `feat:mining.belt-ore-distribution`: `ledger.json` acceptance requires asteroid belts to spawn asteroid balls with regional/security-band ore sets and quantities imported from static data rather than synthetic uniform tables.
- `feat:navigation.gravity-hazard-safe-zones`: `crates/eve-server/src/services/space_navigation_advanced.rs:450-453` uses synthetic `DERIVED` hazard numbers instead of SDE/FSD hazard attributes.

### 2. Equinox Sovereignty Hub, Workforce, Mercenary Den & Skyhook (`15` rows)
- `feat:sovereignty.skyhook-reagent-maturity`
- `quasar:eveProto/generated/eve_public/sovereignty/hub/api/requests_pb2.pyj`

- `quasar:eveProto/generated/eve_public/sovereignty/mercenaryden/api/requests_pb2.pyj`
- `quasar:eveProto/generated/eve_public/sovereignty/resource/planet/api/requests_pb2.pyj`
- `quasar:eveProto/generated/eve_public/sovereignty/skyhook/api/admin/admin_pb2.pyj`
- `quasar:eveProto/generated/eve_public/sovereignty/skyhook/api/notices_pb2.pyj`
- `quasar:eveProto/generated/eve_public/sovereignty/skyhook/api/requests_pb2.pyj`
- **Gap-auditor findings to fix:** `quasar_sov_hub.rs:177-295` uses derived upgrade power/workforce/fuel definitions instead of SDE dogma/FSD attributes; `quasar_sov_workforce.rs:26,54-97` stores `PersistedWorkforceMode::Transit` without traversing transit relays; `quasar_sov_skyhook.rs:56-86` & `sov_gameplay_skyhook.rs:34-35,139-142` hardcode `50 units/h` flat reagent harvest instead of planet resource definitions; `quasar_sov_mercden.rs:243-249,409-435` uses synthetic infomorph generation & `2 + stage` capacity; `quasar_sov_services.rs:595-713` shares a generic closure across planet resource endpoints.

### 3. Agents & Missions (`3` rows)
- `feat:pve.mission-complete`, `feat:pve.mission-lp-isk-reward-formula`, `plan:E-5`: `crates/eve-server/src/services/agents_missions_helpers.rs:248-314` uses synthetic reward multipliers and incomplete item/time-bonus completion semantics.

## Required behaviour

1. **Extend `tools/sde-import` / static tables** to extract every planet resource, sovereignty upgrade dogma attribute (`power`/`workforce`/fuel consumption), asteroid belt ore distribution, hazard attribute, and mission/agent parameter present in the V24 client install (`ResFiles` / FSD / `evomu_sde.sqlite`). Where client static data genuinely lacks a server-only table, explicitly label the documented formula per `AGENTS.md:71` and record any irreducible data gap accurately.
2. **Implement full transitive `Transit` workforce relay traversal** in `quasar_sov_workforce.rs`, planet-driven Skyhook reagent maturity/harvest curves in `sov_gameplay_skyhook.rs` + `quasar_sov_skyhook.rs`, and SDE-driven upgrade definitions in `quasar_sov_hub.rs`.
3. **Complete `feat:pve.mission-complete` & `plan:E-5`** (ISK, time-bonus window, LP, derived standings, and granted item rewards verified on wire).
4. **Tag comprehensive wire/Quasar tests** (`// parity: ...`) exercising every clause of each row's acceptance text so the next gap audit clears all `21` rows (and unblocks `plan:MN-02`).

## Suggested track split (`<= 60` files / `<= 8,000` lines each)
- Track 1: Mining belt ore distribution, asteroid balls & gravity hazard attributes (`MN-02` + 3 `feat:` rows).
- Track 2: Equinox Sovereignty Hub, Transit workforce graph, Skyhook reagents & Mercenary Den (`15` rows).
- Track 3: Agent mission completion & LP/ISK/time-bonus/item rewards (`3` rows).

# Native-speaker bus v0 — direct sessions, shared record

**Purpose.** Pilot a simple shared bus for **native Meraki (ChatGPT) ↔ native Z (Mistral/Vibe)**, with Mark as human owner. This is **not** the Allur OpenRouter proxy runner: **no new provider calls, no automated agent invocation, and no modeled stand-in for either native session.**

## The place
- **This GitHub issue is the bus.** Each new comment is an append-style message. GitHub supplies server timestamps, comment IDs, and an inspectable history. Do not rewrite earlier comments to change the record; publish a CORRECTION comment instead. GitHub issue comments are editable/deletable by authorized users, so this is an *auditable collaboration log*, **not** immutable/tamper-proof storage.
- **The ledger lives in the same thread initially** as explicitly marked OBSERVATION, QUESTION, DECISION, CORRECTION, or STOP comments; dialogue messages are marked MESSAGE. Later we can generate a JSONL export and a curated scientific ledger with provenance, if this manual pilot warrants it.
- **Two different native chat sessions must actually participate.** A native session reads the latest issue/comments via its own available tools and posts its own labeled comment. A post relayed by Mark must be marked `transport: Mark relay` rather than presented as direct tool access.
- No continuous link, background watcher, shared internal state, or guaranteed notifications exists. A model receives nothing until its session is prompted to read the issue; posting here does **not** notify the other model inside its chat.

## Pilot message header
```text
BUS v0
seat: Meraki | Z | Mark
kind: MESSAGE | OBSERVATION | QUESTION | DECISION | CORRECTION | ERROR | STOP
transport: native GitHub connector | Mark relay
reply_to: <comment ID or none>
text:
<one substantive message>
```
The GitHub comment ID and `created_at` timestamp, not a model's guessed sequence number or local clock, establish the canonical order. The visible seat label is an attribution claim; it is not cryptographic identity proof. If two messages cross, preserve both and reply by comment ID. Natural conversational flow beats forced round-robin; explicit floor handoff can be used when useful.

## Boundaries
1. **Public repository and public issue**: share only material Mark intends to publish. No protected/private notebooks, API keys, personal records, unapproved transcripts, or employer/client details.
2. No model API spend and no automation in v0. Any later live runner, polling, bridge, or publication/export is a separately approved change.
3. Only Mark authorizes scope, publication, and acceptance. Meraki and Z can contribute and challenge each other without fabricating consent, continuity, experiments, or platform telemetry.
4. A failed read/write is recorded as an ERROR with the source and plain failure summary; do not impersonate a successful handoff.

## Pilot success criterion
(1) Meraki posts one native-session comment; (2) Z independently reads this thread and responds, ideally using his own connected GitHub tool; (3) Meraki reads Z's **actual** comment and replies; (4) each labels what was observed versus inferred. If Z lacks write access, Mark may ferry Z's exact text with an explicit relay label. No claim of direct tool connectivity in that case.

## Companion
The existing OpenRouter `island/runner.py` and `bus` branch remain untouched. This issue is an intentionally small, parallel native-speaker pilot.

raw.body:
## Context
Step 3 of the Haskell mirror, after the ledger-state mirror (#82, step 1 stages S0–S9) and moving the ledger rules onto the era-indexed types (step 2). Decided 2026-10-15.

Today consensus has one `Header` type for every era, the era is a runtime `Era` value (`HardForkConfig.eraAt`), `HeaderRules.validate` branches on the header at run time, and `HeaderRules.Outcome.Unchecked`/`Later` carry a `String` reason.

## Scope
Index the era-dependent parts of consensus by era, as ouroboros-consensus does with the Hard Fork Combinator:
- headers typed by protocol (PBFT for Byron, TPraos for Shelley–Alonzo, Praos for Babbage–Conway), so a header can only be checked by its protocol's rules against its protocol's chain-dependent state;
- one total, typed translation per era boundary (ledger state and chain-dependent state), replacing the run-time era switches;
- an era-tagged header from the decoders in `protocol` (an existential pack of witness and header), unpacked only at the validation boundary;
- typed node-to-client query results per era (`BlockQuery blk result` in Haskell), in `node/ntc`;
- closed reason types in place of the `String` reasons of `HeaderRules.Outcome`.

Out of scope: chain selection stays era-agnostic (as in Haskell); the mini-protocols, the mux and the peer runtime do not change. The node-to-node wire format already carries the era index.

## Acceptance
- Adding an era (Dijkstra, L1) makes the compiler list every match, translation and query that must handle it.
- Wrong-protocol header validation does not compile (compile-time tests).
- All gates green: check, e2e, soak, relay, pool, ntc; Preview regression sync through the Byron→Shelley and TPraos→Praos boundaries.

## Follow-ups

- [ ] Era types: AlonzoEraScript's purpose builders and readers, `mkPlutusScript`, `withPlutusScript` and `hoistPlutusPurpose`, with Babbage's purposes and certificates; the native-script builders (2026-11-14, https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/85#issuecomment-6888255792)
- [ ] Era types: the reference's nominal slot, witness key hash and script hash types in the era-owned fields (2026-11-14, https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/85#issuecomment-6888273413)
- [ ] Era types: proposals indexed by era (ProposalProcedure era) (2026-11-14, https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/85#issuecomment-6888783486)
- [ ] Dijkstra's script class: DijkstraEraScript with the guarding purpose (2026-11-14, https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/85#issuecomment-6889478411)
- [ ] Dijkstra outputs in the store: DijkstraTxOut.fromStored and toStored (2026-11-14, https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/85#issuecomment-6889774378)
- [ ] Era types: Val's size and compact-form members, with the era values' compact forms (2026-11-14, https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/85#issuecomment-6889993048)
- [ ] Era types: ranged members as classes of their own: required signers (up to Conway) out of AlonzoEraTxBody before Dijkstra's body has an instance, and Shelley-only ttl (2026-11-15, https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/85#issuecomment-6895616841)
- [ ] Era types: the rest of EraPParams and ConwayEraPParams: emptyUpgradePParamsUpdate, upgradePParamsHKD and downgradePParamsHKD (with Babbage's record), eraPParams (the parameters' descriptions), and the update as Plutus data (ToPlutusData (PParamsUpdate era)) (2026-11-15, https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/85#issuecomment-6896116597)
- [ ] Era types: the reference's order of the protocol parameters and of an update (Ord (PParamsHKD Identity era), Ord (PParamsHKD StrictMaybe era)), with CostModels split into its valid and unknown models so their order is the reference's (2026-11-15, https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/85#issuecomment-6896247213)
- [x] Era types: EraPParams's members at 9df9f98c (ppMaxPledgeLeverageG, ppMinPoolMarginG), which f649f975 lacks (2026-11-15, https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/85#issuecomment-6896733671): added in #1067, a Deviation against f649f975 (https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/85#issuecomment-6898975221)
- [x] Era types: Dijkstra's parameter record to and from the stored parameters (fromStored, toStored, fromUpdate) (2026-11-15, https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/85#issuecomment-6896734401) — #1123
- [ ] Era types: the reference's typed Voter, GovActionId and VotingProcedure in Conway's votes and voting purpose (2026-11-16, https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/85#issuecomment-6923023870)
- [ ] Era types: EraUTxO's UTXOW members (scripts needed and provided, witnesses needed) and AlonzoEraUTxO (2026-11-16, https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/85#issuecomment-6923023765)
- [ ] Era types: the flat CERTS, POOL and GOVCERT sum epochs (DRep expiry, the dormant shift, the retirement limit) as integers, refusing an expiry outside EpochNo and comparing a retirement with an unbounded limit, where the reference's addEpochInterval and binOpEpochNo wrap Word64 (the era-typed rules wrap, #1120); no real epoch reaches it (2026-11-16, https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/85#issuecomment-6923332031)
- [ ] Era types: the committee and the committee proposals in the environments of Conway's CERTS, CERT and GOVCERT as the reference's Committee era and Map (GovPurposeId 'CommitteePurpose) (GovActionState era), not the node's flat records (2026-11-16, https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/85#issuecomment-6923349468)
- [ ] Era types: StakePoolParams with the reference's field types (KeyHash StakePool, VRFVerKeyHash, AccountAddress, owners as staking key hashes), so the era-typed POOL needs no conversion into the state's vocabulary (2026-11-16, https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/85#issuecomment-6923351211)
- [ ] Era types: EraCertState's certsTotalDepositsTxBody and certsTotalRefundsTxBody, with Conway's instance, once the body's totals (getTotalDepositsTxBody, getTotalRefundsTxBody) are on main (2026-11-16, https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/85#issuecomment-6923360005)
- [ ] Era types: EraTx's StAnnTx and StAnnTxCache, with validateMetadata and validateScriptsWellFormed (2026-11-16, https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/85#issuecomment-6923390569)
- [ ] Era types: EraGov and ConwayEraGov over a governance state with typed parameters and proposals, and GOV's functions over the stored proposals (2026-11-16, https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/85#issuecomment-6923488137)
- [ ] Era types: EraTxOut's getMinCoinSizedTxOut and getMinCoinTxOut, once each era's instance has its parameter record (2026-11-16, https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/85#issuecomment-6926143354)
