raw.body:
Itens de roadmap de design e personagem.

Consolida issues menores (uma por achado) num checklist único. PR de correção usa `Refs #<esta>` e marca o item; esta issue fecha quando o checklist inteiro estiver feito.

- [ ] Roadmap: turntable 3D da Kairya com o asset real (era #174)
  **Parado (14/11):** a geração do modelo 3D é paga, e nenhuma operação paga entra sem aprovação do responsável pelo projeto. Sem PR até essa aprovação.
  <details><summary>Contexto original</summary>

  ## Objetivo
  
  Trocar o placeholder da recompensa de nível novo pelo turntable real da Kairya. O pipeline local (Blender e codificação), o componente `KairyaTurntable`, o botão de pausa (WCAG 2.2.2) e o E2E já estão na `main`. Falta gerar o modelo e ligar o asset.
  
  ## Tarefas
  
  - [ ] Gerar o modelo 3D a partir do retrato aprovado, com aprovação prévia do dono. Custo a confirmar antes de gerar.
  - [ ] Baixar o GLB para `assets-src/3d/kairya.glb` e rodar o pipeline local (`scripts/kairya_turntable.py` e `encode-turntable.sh`).
  - [ ] Conferir os tetos de tamanho: webm até 1,5 MiB e poster webp até 200 KiB.
  - [ ] Ligar a constante `TURNTABLE` no front.
  - [ ] Ajustar `turntable.test.ts`, o teste "sem asset" do `KairyaTurntable` e os testes de nível novo do `RewardAnnouncement` (stub de `matchMedia`).
  - [ ] Garantir que o E2E de movimento reduzido distingue vídeo de poster.
  - [ ] Registrar procedência do asset em `docs/ART.md`.
  
  ## Critério de pronto
  
  - O nível novo mostra o vídeo em loop com pausa ou, sob `prefers-reduced-motion`, só o poster; em falha de carregamento volta ao placeholder.
  - axe sem violações nos dois cenários.
  - `make check` e o quality-gate verdes.
  
  ## Dependências
  
  - Retrato da Kairya aprovado (entregue).
  - Aprovação do dono para a geração paga.

  </details>
- [ ] Roadmap: migrar as telas para os componentes do design system (era #173)
  <details><summary>Contexto original</summary>

  ## Objetivo
  
  Levar as telas existentes para os componentes base de `frontend/src/shared/ui/`. Os tokens, a tipografia e os componentes já estão na `main`, mas várias telas ainda usam `<button>` e marcação própria. A etapa também entrega o único movimento orquestrado previsto no design: a lanterna que acende ao concluir a diária.
  
  ## Tarefas
  
  Um PR por área:
  
  - [x] Missões: `CycleSection`, `EvaluationPanel`, `EvidenceForm`, `MissionCard`, `MissionList` e `RescheduleForm` passam a usar `Button`, `IconButton`, `Field`, `Panel`, `StatusLine` e `ConfirmDialog`. — resolvido no PR #216
  - [x] Progressão: `ProgressPanel` passa a usar `Panel`, `ProgressBar` e `Badge`. — resolvido no PR #217
  - [x] Tutoria: `DecisionControls`, `TutorConversation` e `TutorPanel` passam a usar os componentes base. — resolvido nos PRs #218 e #219
  - [x] Animação da lanterna acesa (cerca de 900 ms) ao concluir a diária, desligada sob `prefers-reduced-motion`.
  - [x] Testes de unidade e axe nos estados de cada tela migrada, com a cobertura do front em 100%. #221 pôs na galeria axe o reagendamento e a evidência; #222, a recusa no DecisionControls e o aviso de cópia do plano da semana; #223, o quadro de missões com os estados do cartão. — resolvido nos PRs #221, #222 e #223
  
  ## Critério de pronto
  
  - Nenhuma tela de feature usa `<button>` cru nem estilo arbitrário fora dos componentes.
  - As telas fazem o mesmo que antes e mantêm os textos (refactor puro, exceto a animação nova).
  - Contraste e foco visível conferidos pelos testes existentes; axe sem violações nas duas línguas.
  - `make check` e o quality-gate verdes.
  
  ## Dependências
  
  - Tokens, tipografia e componentes base do design system (entregues).

  </details>
- [ ] Roadmap: contract dos valores legados da personagem (era #172)
  **Parado (14/11):** depende da conferência em produção de que a migração `0008` (expand + backfill) está implantada e de que não há linha com valor legado. Sem PR até essa conferência.
  <details><summary>Contexto original</summary>

  ## Objetivo
  
  Fechar o expand/contract da troca de nome da mentora. A migração de expand e o backfill já estão na `main`: o banco grava só `kairya` e `kairya_partnership`, mas os CHECKs ainda aceitam os valores legados e o domínio ainda os normaliza na leitura (tolerant reader). Esta etapa remove essa tolerância.
  
  ## Tarefas
  
  - [ ] Nova migração Alembic de contract: os CHECKs das colunas de origem do reagendamento e de código de conquista passam a aceitar só os valores novos.
  - [ ] `downgrade` que restaura os CHECKs expandidos.
  - [ ] Remover o tolerant reader de `src/focusquest/modules/missions/models.py` e de `src/focusquest/modules/progression/models.py`.
  - [ ] Teste de integração: inserir um valor legado depois do `upgrade` gera violação de CHECK.
  - [ ] Teste de integração: `downgrade` → `upgrade` idempotente.
  - [ ] Registrar a decisão no handoff do PR.
  
  ## Critério de pronto
  
  - Nenhum valor legado é aceito pelo banco nem pelo domínio.
  - `test_sem_franquia.py` e o teste de paridade entre modelo e esquema migrado continuam verdes.
  - `make check` e o quality-gate verdes.
  
  ## Dependências
  
  - Exige que a migração de expand (`0008`) já esteja implantada em produção antes do merge, para não haver linha legada sem backfill.

  </details>

- [ ] Varredura de falhas (14/11/2026; setecentas e duas rodadas, gitleaks sem achados em todo o histórico, nenhum segredo real)

  - [ ] Dependências vulneráveis no `uv.lock`: `opentelemetry-api` 1.45.0 vai para produção (CVE-2026-114603 e CVE-2026-126360; corrigido na 1.45.2). Só em dev: `virtualenv` 21.14.5, `filelock` 4.0.10 e `certifi` 2026.7.22 (corrigidos em 21.14.9, 4.2.1 e 2026.10.18). No `frontend/package-lock.json`, só em dev e no CI: `npm audit` acusa 16 (4 high), entre elas `vite` 8.3.0 (`launch-editor`), `undici` via `jsdom`, `zod` via `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` e `@vitest/mocker`; `npm audit fix` resolve dentro das faixas atuais. Complemento: `npm audit`/`uv audit` não cobrem os pacotes do sistema das bases Debian e Alpine; nada no repositório faz scan do digest publicado (Trivy ou Grype, falhando em HIGH/CRITICAL com correção), que entraria como alvo do Makefile com o job correspondente. Complemento: o `opentelemetry-api` não é dependência direta: entra como transitiva do `fastapi` (`uv.lock:265`) e nada o instrumenta, então a correção é `uv lock --upgrade-package opentelemetry-api`, não remover o pacote.
  - [ ] Testes frágeis: espera fixa de 20 ms para afirmar ausência (`useMissions.test.tsx:169`, `TutorPanel.test.tsx:530`, `useTutorConversation.test.tsx:92`, `useTutorStatus.test.tsx:86,129`); E2E serial com estado de módulo (`cycle.spec.ts:70-81`; `cycle-midnight`, `presenca` e `week-plan` sem reset por teste); E2E: backdrop achado por classes Tailwind (`tutor-focus.spec.ts:328`) e legenda lida uma vez com `textContent()` antes de aparecer (`presenca.spec.ts:139`, `audio.spec.ts:192`), o que deixa o `not.toHaveText` da linha 147 passar sem provar nada; `datetime.now` em helpers de integração (`tests/integration/camada3*.py`, `test_acompanhamento_concorrencia.py`). Backend: testes de integração que só conferem o status, sem o `code` nem o efeito (`test_iniciar_missao.py:428`, `test_tutoring_teto_diario.py:216-227`, `test_cycle_api.py:281,311`), e datas de fixture com relógio real (`datetime.now` em `test_acompanhamento_concorrencia.py:260`, `test_missions_concorrencia.py:97`, `test_missions_api.py:210,647`), que podem falhar perto da meia-noite. Unidade: a curva de XP só é testada como crescente e positiva (`test_missions_domain.py:70-78`), e `test_cycle_domain.py:407` e `test_missions_api.py:251` calculam o esperado com o próprio `xp_para_dificuldade` (usar tabela literal); faltam as fronteiras `agora == prazo` em `na_conclusao_tardia` e `prazo - 1µs` em `com_inicio_a_tempo`, e cenários de `maior_sequencia` com dia sem plano; `problema_do_novo_prazo` (`missions/domain.py:252`) confere `tzinfo is None` em vez de `utcoffset() is None`, como as outras guardas.; `MissionList.test.tsx:2474` devolve duas missões com o mesmo id (aviso de key `7`, só a fixture) e o T7 (`:1051`) termina sem esperar a recarga (aviso de `act`) Complemento: 15 ausências afirmadas depois de `setTimeout(resolve, 0)` (`useCycle.test.tsx:633`, `LanternTrail.test.tsx:173`, `useProgress.test.tsx:478`), trocar por `flushPendingEffects()` ou `waitFor`; `KairyaTurntable.test.tsx:198-203` ainda espia o `catch` da promise e afirma `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)`, preso à implementação. Também `serial` sem motivo em `evaluation.spec.ts:57` e `tracking.spec.ts:156`: ambos reiniciam o estado em `beforeEach` e o config já tem `workers: 1`, então o `serial` só faz uma falha no primeiro teste de `tracking` pular os seguintes; remover o `mode: 'serial'`.
  - [ ] Fronteira de tipos no frontend: `client.ts:228` converte a resposta com `as T`, sem parse (afeta os 8 hooks de dados); `!` em refs em `CycleSection.tsx`, `TutorPanel.tsx`, `useTutorConversation.ts` e `Headquarters.tsx`; listener de `error` de `audioPlayer.ts:74` nunca é removido. O `postStream` (`client.ts:582`) não tem prazo até os cabeçalhos, não tem watchdog de inatividade na leitura e não limita o tamanho do `buffer`: com a conexão meio aberta, a conversa fica em "enviando" até desmontar. Robustez no runtime: o `translate` lança no render quando falta uma variável, e não existe nenhum `ErrorBoundary` (`catalog.ts:49`; é preciso tipar as variáveis por chave e pôr um boundary na raiz). `useProgress.ts:82` e `useCycle.ts:81` não invalidam o `requestId` na limpeza, ao contrário de `useMissions.ts:165`. `useRefreshOnReturn.ts:59-60` duplica GETs com `focus` + `visibilitychange`. A chave `focusquest.tutor-panel.open` está fora do namespace `kairyaquest.*`. Consequência concreta na trilha das Campanhas: `LANTERN_STATE` (`lanterns.ts:14`) e `DAY_TEXT`/`SPECIAL_TEXT` (`LanternTrail.tsx:24-40`) não tratam disponibilidade desconhecida (classe CSS `"undefined"` e texto sem chave). Complemento: ao renomear, migrar o valor antigo na primeira leitura e apagar a chave velha dentro do `try`, com teste (`focusquest.tutor-panel.open = 'false'` → `readPanelOpen()` `false`, chave nova `'false'`, antiga `null`) e a constante conferida com literal fixo como em `soundPrefs.test.ts:20`; o `panelPreference.test.ts` também não cobre o getter de `window.localStorage` lançando, que os outros módulos cobrem (`useDailyOpening.test.tsx:223`).
  - [ ] Higiene de infraestrutura: `postgres:18.6-alpine` sem digest em `compose.yaml` e `quality.yml`; Dockerfiles sem `HEALTHCHECK` (ou registrar que a plataforma faz a probe); `|| true` em `scripts/novo-worktree.sh:290-291`; `npm ci` do CI sem `--ignore-scripts` (`quality.yml:66,169`; a imagem já usa); `push` sem filtro de branch roda o gate duas vezes por commit de PR e a `concurrency` descarta a publicação do commit intermediário em dois merges seguidos (`quality.yml:3-15`); `type: ignore[arg-type]` sem justificativa escrita em `test_cycle_models.py:121` (os `noqa: F401` e os `type: ignore[prop-decorator]` já são justificados).
  - [x] `lanternReveal.ts`: o comentário e a nota do handoff atribuem ao render duplo do StrictMode um risco que não se reproduz no React 19. Corrigir o motivo e acrescentar um teste que reprove a gravação no render. (#221)
  - [ ] Lógica de negócio do backend: o `comeback` (R4) conta os dias pela data de `completed_at` (`progression/service.py:351-359`), então uma conclusão tardia depois da meia-noite concede a conquista com só 2 dias sem conclusão, e falta o teste desse caso; o reenvio do reagendamento compara só `(new_deadline, reason)` e ignora a origem (`missions/service.py:440`); há `assert falha is not None` em caminho de produção (`evaluation/service.py:134`), que some com `python -O`; `preparar_turno` (`tutoring/service.py:211`) trava o usuário com `FOR UPDATE` simples, que bloqueia os INSERTs com FK para `users` enquanto dura, quando a outra trava de `users` (`progression/service.py:117`) usa `key_share=True`. As chaves de operação (`mission_operations.operation_id`, `tutor_actions.operation_id` e `client_message_id`) são únicas no sistema inteiro, e não por usuário: o 409 `operacao_reutilizada` revela que a chave existe com outro dono. Levar para `(user_id, operation_id)` com expand/contract, como já faz `idempotency_keys`. raw.body:
# [RFC] Support MiniCPM-o 4.5 streaming duplex GRPO training

## Summary

This RFC proposes a streaming **full-duplex GRPO** training pipeline for MiniCPM-o 4.5 on verl-omni, with vLLM-Omni as the rollout engine.

The goal is **capability verification, not model-performance SOTA**: prove that verl-omni can run policy optimization over real full-duplex sessions — time-aligned trajectory capture, actor/rollout log-probability parity on streaming actions, event-driven loss masking, temporal rule rewards, and weight sync between duplex rollout batches — at PoC scale (one 4×H800 node, under 10 GB of training data).

This concretizes the duplex GRPO track (Phase 2–3) of the parent RFC #345 with a minimal, evidence-based design. The simplex OPD foundation (#565) has landed; duplex DPO and duplex OPD are explicitly out of scope here and build on the same trajectory contract later (the streaming duplex OPD track is #566). Roadmap context: #700 ("MiniCPM-o, streaming & duplex RL").

Design principles, in order:

1. **Keep the algorithm surface simple.** GRPO as already implemented in verl/verl-omni, plus CPU rule rewards computed from timestamps and VAD.
2. **Replay, not closed loop.** Training episodes are short event-typed segments replayed from a two-track corpus. This follows the only replicated duplex-RL result (Kyutai's interactivity alignment, arXiv 2606.11167), which trains on pre-recorded segments and generalizes to real-time evaluation.
3. **Preserve the checkpoint.** This is real post-training on top of the released checkpoint's existing duplex behavior. A reward-calibration entry gate, KL regularization, LoRA, and regression trip-wires keep the base policy's strength intact and keep initial rewards at reasonable mid-band values instead of near-zero floors.

## 1. Motivation

verl-omni currently trains omni-modal models as bounded, turn-based prompt/response rollouts. A full-duplex model like MiniCPM-o 4.5 continuously listens and watches while it speaks; turn-taking, pause retention, and barge-in yielding are decided by the model itself every second. Treating such a session as an ordinary prompt plus response loses the timing, the interleaving of input and output, and the causal link between newly arriving user audio and concurrently generated tokens.

The missing framework capability is the object of this RFC: **on-policy RL over streaming duplex trajectories**. MiniCPM-o 4.5 is the reference model because its checkpoint, duplex inference code, and a production duplex runtime in vLLM-Omni are already open.

What already exists and is reused:

| Layer | Status | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MiniCPM-o thinker training on verl-omni | Validated: GSPO LoRA recipe on AVQA (sync and separate-async variants, CI smoke), offline omni DPO (#550), simplex OPD (#565, merged as #858) | `examples/gspo_trainer/minicpm/`, `examples/dpo_trainer/minicpm/`, `examples/opd_trainer/minicpm_o/` |
| Omni adapter registries | Merged (#232 lineage): `OmniModelBase`, `OmniRolloutPipelineBase`, per-adapter `pipeline_mode` vocabularies | `verl_omni/pipelines/model_base.py` |
| MiniCPM-o duplex rollout runtime | Merged in vLLM-Omni (PR #3907 lineage): session open/append/signal, 1 s unit ingestion, listen/speak control, barge-in, in-process async API | `vllm_omni/engine/duplex*`, `vllm_omni/model_executor/models/minicpmo_4_5/` |
| Prompt/media parity discipline | Merged: actor/rollout/teacher render identical media spans | `verl_omni/pipelines/minicpm/prompt_parity.py` |

What is missing and owned by this RFC:

- Per-token log-probabilities and deterministic token capture from the vLLM-Omni duplex samplers (today the duplex paths set `logprobs_tensors=None`).
- A duplex trajectory contract, replay/collation into training batches, and event-driven masks (`verl_omni/utils/dataset/duplex/` is greenfield).
- A `pipeline_mode="duplex"` rollout bridge in `verl_omni/pipelines/minicpm/` (the adapter currently implements `thinker_only` only).
- Event-typed replay datasets, temporal rule rewards, and duplex-specific training telemetry.

## 2. MiniCPM-o 4.5 duplex mechanics that shape the design

From the released remote code and the vLLM-Omni runtime (verified against the `openbmb/MiniCPM-o-4_5` snapshot and the vLLM-Omni tree):

- The interaction is cut into **1 s units**. Each unit is `<unit>` + (optional) one vision block (`<image>` + 64 resampler embeddings + `</image>`) + 10 pooled audio embeddings, followed by the model's output tokens for that unit, then `</unit>`.
- The model decides **whether to speak** by sampling control tokens (`<|listen|>` / `<|speak|>`) and **what to say** via at most 20 text tokens per unit, terminated early by sampled terminators (`<|chunk_eos|>`, `<|turn_eos|>`).
- **Barge-in is model-owned.** User audio arriving while the model speaks is ingested natively; yielding means the model itself emits `<|turn_eos|>` then `<|listen|>`. No external VAD or runtime cancellation is required for the behavior to exist.
- Sampling is **two-stage**: a boundary draw decides `<|chunk_eos|>` on the raw distribution, then the content token is drawn after a forbidden-id mask (including a 6,965-id `bad_token_ids` list), repetition penalty 1.05 over a 512-token window, and temperature/top-k/top-p truncation (defaults 0.7/100/0.8).
- Speech rendering is a **separate policy**: the MiniCPMTTS decoder consumes LLM hidden states and emits codec tokens, then token2wav synthesizes audio. This RFC freezes it; gradients flow on LLM text/control tokens only. This also matches the published finding that objectives restricted to text tokens are stable where full-stream objectives degrade (RL evidence in arXiv 2606.11167; preference-alignment evidence in arXiv 2506.21463).

## 3. Design

### 3.1 Environment: two-track replay, event-typed segments

Episodes are 3–5 s event-typed segments mined from a stereo two-track corpus using word-level timestamps: **pause** (user intra-utterance silence; model must stay silent), **turn** (user utterance ends; model should take the floor), and **interruption** (user speech starts while the model speaks; model should yield promptly). Interruption segments are constructed by overlapping the two tracks, with injection keyed to the model's speak onset; the taxonomy follows Full-Duplex-Bench and arXiv 2606.11167. Group members can therefore see slightly different injection timings; this divergence is accepted for replay construction.

Each episode runs as a real duplex session in vLLM-Omni: the user track is fed chunk-by-chunk at the native 1 s cadence, the model generates concurrently, and sessions are bounded (segment + up to 30 s context). The user track's content never reacts to the policy.

The harness never cancels model output. There is no forced truncation of the model's speech; yielding is the model's own decision and is scored post-hoc. This keeps every sampled token a genuine policy action.

### 3.2 Trajectory contract and transport

A rollout produces a `DuplexTrajectory`: time-ordered events carrying input chunks (modality, timestamps, engine-computed unit embeddings and text token ids), model actions (per-unit token ids, log-probabilities, validity mask, per-session sampling parameters), terminators, and engine-forcing markers.

Transport follows the validated qwen3_tts pattern exactly: at `postprocess_agent_loop_output` the structured trajectory converts into the standard `AgentLoopOutput` shape plus one namespaced `extra_fields` replay key. No new batch format; verl's rectangular batches and `response_mask` machinery are reused.

The validity mask is **0 only for engine/env-forced tokens**: cap-resolved `<|chunk_eos|>`, mid-turn `<|listen|>`→`<|tts_bos|>` rewrites, explicit `force_listen`, and the implicit listen-forcing of silent units after `<|turn_eos|>`. All sampled tokens — including tokens generated after an interruption — carry mask 1. Forced and rewritten tokens are excluded from loss and importance ratios.

### 3.3 Log-probability contract

The engine emits log-probabilities of the **exact distribution the runtime sampled**: stage-1 Bernoulli on `<|chunk_eos|>` over the raw softmax, and stage-2 draws after the forbidden mask, repetition penalty, and truncation. Trainer-side recomputation (old log-probs, reference KL) uses the same post-truncation distribution; the repetition-penalty history is reconstructible from the trajectory's token ids, and per-session sampling parameters are recorded in the trajectory.

### 3.4 Rollout bridge

`verl_omni/pipelines/minicpm/` gains `pipeline_mode="duplex"` beside `thinker_only`, cloning the same thinker stage with the duplex runtime and driving vLLM-Omni's in-process `DuplexOmni` session API.

vLLM-Omni work items (small, model-scoped, upstreamable):

- Emit log-probabilities from the MiniCPM-o duplex stage-0 samplers (the two-stage path already exists; the samplers currently return `logprobs_tensors=None`), carried through the existing segment metadata surfaces.
- Deterministic per-session capture: sampled token ids, unit boundaries, unit embeddings, terminators, forcing markers, sampling parameters.

Weight-update fencing is not needed at this scale: under the colocated sync trainer, generation drains before `update_weights`. Two invariants are pinned: pre-warming opens sessions only (open performs no forward), and any session that has appended data closes before the next weight sync.

### 3.5 Algorithm: GRPO with simple rule rewards

- **Optimizer**: GRPO (arXiv 2402.03300) as implemented in verl-omni (`adv_estimator: grpo`), sequence-level group advantage per segment, group size ≈16, clipping ε=0.2, text-token loss.
- **KL**: on by default, small β, against the starting checkpoint (the validated AVQA recipe runs KL off; for duplex we default on as a behavior-preservation guard).
- **Rewards** (CPU, rule-based, from VAD/timestamps; fixed weights):
  - Pause violation: −1 if the model speaks inside a tagged pause window, else 0.
  - Turn latency: −(delay from user turn end to model speech start), with a tuned full-credit band.
  - Interruption yield: −(delay from the end of the user's interrupting speech to the model's return to silence), with a tuned deadline.
- **Telemetry in-loop**: per-axis turn-taking/overlap rates, silence share, duplicate n-gram share, speak ratio — rule-reward degeneracy (silence collapse, repetition) is the documented failure mode of duplex RL (arXiv 2604.10065; arXiv 2606.11167), so the trip-wires are part of the training loop, not an afterthought.
- Reward scorers are registered through the existing reward manager and aligned with the #723 layered-scorer direction so the ongoing reward refactor does not rework the semantics.

### 3.6 Preserve-the-policy requirements

- **Reward-calibration entry gate**: before any gradient step, the unmodified starting checkpoint is rolled over the mined event set. Per-axis reward distributions must land in a sane mid band (target: mean normalized reward ≥ ~0.4 of axis maximum). If an axis floors the base model, the event construction or reward band is misaligned with the checkpoint's actual behavior and must be fixed before training. This guarantees initial rewards are reasonable rather than near-zero, and that training refines existing behavior instead of rebuilding it.
- LoRA plus frozen audio/vision towers (the validated recipe pattern).
- Regression gate with pre-registered thresholds: AVQA accuracy-reward drop > 5% relative blocks a run; telemetry trip-wires (duplicate n-gram share ceiling, silence-share ceiling, speak-ratio band) block on breach.

### 3.7 Data

Single training corpus: **`kyutai/DailyTalkContiguous`** (2,541 dialogues, ~22 h, stereo two-track with word-level timestamps, CC-BY-SA-4.0; based on DailyTalk, arXiv 2207.01063). As distributed it is ~12 GB of 44.1 kHz-class stereo WAV; the ingestion pipeline is 16 kHz-native, so the stored working set is ~5 GB — within the PoC budget. Word-level timestamps support mining pause and turn segments directly; 22 h yields on the order of 10–20 k minable segments, consistent with published duplex-RL data scales (arXiv 2606.11167 trains on ≤2 k segments per axis). Interruptions are constructed by track overlap. The corpus is scripted read speech, so natural backchannels are absent: the backchannel axis is out of the PoC and deferred to the scale-up tier.

- Regression data: an AVQA subset (the validated in-repo recipe data).
- Evaluation: Full-Duplex-Bench v1 static protocol, restricted to its rule-based timing metrics (github.com/DanielLin94144/Full-Duplex-Bench).
- Scale-up corpora (DuplexConv, Seamless Interaction) are explicitly out of the PoC.

### 3.8 Compute topology and pacing

One node, 4×H800, colocated sync trainer — exactly the validated AVQA recipe topology (rollout TP=2, LoRA merge, gradient checkpointing, actor/reference parameter offload available). Episodes are bounded (≤ ~35 s ≈ ~3.5 k LLM positions).

Pacing rules that are correctness requirements, not optimizations: every concurrent session's next chunk submit must beat the 1 s unit deadline (the runtime's silence-continuation clock otherwise injects unscheduled silent units); session open is cheap after engine warmup (the cold open is once per engine); the pre-warm pool follows the §3.4 invariants.

One sizing note: at the model's 1 Hz decision cadence a 3–5 s segment contains only ~3–5 listen/speak decisions (12.5 Hz-codec models have ~12× more per segment), so group sizes and segment counts are scaled accordingly.

## 4. Implementation plan

| Phase | Deliverables | Exit criteria |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **M0 — parity spike** | vLLM-Omni: duplex-sampler log-prob emission + deterministic capture. verl-omni: `DuplexTrajectory` contract, `<unit>`-window replay/collation, actor forward parity extending `prompt_parity`, CPU tests | Fixed segments replay deterministically (fixed batch composition, per-request seeded generators); actor-recomputed log-probs match engine log-probs within tolerance on all sampled tokens; every engine-forced token class identified and masked; GPU parity check scripted |
| **M1 — duplex GRPO loop** | Event-mining dataloader, base-policy calibration audit, rule rewards, telemetry + trip-wires, minimal FDB-v1 harness, GRPO LoRA recipe on 4×H800 | Calibration audit passes (mid-band base rewards); a stable short run: rewards flow, no collapse, weight sync between duplex batches, FDB-v1 harness executes, ≥1 timing-axis reward trend improves over the calibrated base; AVQA gate green |

Future work on the same trajectory contract, not in this RFC: duplex DPO, duplex OPD (#566), LLM-judge rewards, backchannel axis, vision-in-episodes, GSPO ablation, long-lived sessions across weight sync, and scale-up corpora.

Task checklist:

vLLM-Omni:
- [ ] Emit two-stage log-probabilities from the MiniCPM-o duplex stage-0 samplers, on the post-mask post-truncation distribution
- [ ] Deterministic per-session capture: token ids, unit boundaries/embeddings, terminators, forcing markers, sampling parameters

verl-omni:
- [ ] `verl_omni/utils/dataset/duplex/`: trajectory contract, replay, collation, schema validation
- [ ] `pipeline_mode="duplex"` rollout bridge in `verl_omni/pipelines/minicpm/`
- [ ] Parity test extending `prompt_parity`; CPU tests for serialization, masks, forced-token taxonomy
- [ ] DailyTalkContiguous event-mining dataloader (pause/turn/constructed interruption) + calibration audit tooling
- [ ] Per-axis rule reward scorers + training telemetry + trip-wires
- [ ] Minimal Full-Duplex-Bench v1 harness (rule metrics)
- [ ] GRPO LoRA duplex recipe (4×H800 colocated) + smoke/e2e tests + docs

## 5. Validation

- CPU: trajectory serialization, `<unit>` window collation, validity-mask taxonomy, reward computation on synthetic timelines, calibration audit logic.
- GPU parity (M0 gate): actor vs engine log-probabilities on fixed segments, including a barge-in episode.
- E2E smoke: duplex rollout → trajectory → reward → GRPO update → weight sync → second duplex rollout.
- Short convergence run with telemetry; regression gate vs the starting checkpoint on the AVQA subset.
- Determinism scope: fixed batch composition with per-request seeded generators (batch-invariance is a separate open upstream concern).

## 6. Risks and mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- |
| Rule-reward degeneracy (repetition in arXiv 2604.10065, silence collapse in arXiv 2606.11167 ablations) | Text-token-only loss, in-loop telemetry with pre-registered trip-wires, calibrated mid-band starting rewards, action-space projection (per ASPIRin) kept as a documented fallback |
| Actor/rollout log-prob mismatch from streaming-vs-offline feature differences | Trajectory carries engine-computed unit embeddings; parity is on inputs by construction and covers sampler/numeric drift only |
| Throughput: many short sessions, 1 s submit deadlines | Pacing rules in §3.8, pre-warmed session pool, throughput arithmetic (sessions/step × open+run ÷ admission limit) included in the recipe docs |
| Upstream coupling on vLLM-Omni sampler changes | Small model-scoped PRs; fork acceptable for the spike; parity test catches drift |
| Duplex loss-mask conventions of the checkpoint are undocumented (which positions are supervised) | M0 reverse-engineers and pins them empirically against the released checkpoint before any training |
| Scripted corpus weakens pause statistics vs spontaneous speech | Accepted for capability verification; scale-up corpora named for the next tier |

## 7. Alternatives considered

- **Closed-loop training with a user simulator or dynamic barge-in injection**: rejected for the core path. Every published duplex-RL result trains on replayed two-track segments; reactive-user effects are out of distribution for any open corpus. Reserved for a later milestone.
- **GSPO as the default optimizer**: GSPO remains available as an ablation, but published duplex RL results use GRPO with text-token restriction, so GRPO is the default here.
- **LLM-judge or learned rewards**: deferred to later milestones; rule rewards are sufficient for this one.
- **Full-stream (codec-token) policy gradients**: deferred. The codec decoder is a separate policy; freezing it matches both the architecture and the published stability evidence.

## 8. Relation to other issues

- #345 — parent umbrella RFC; this RFC concretizes its Phase 2–3 (duplex trajectory bridge + duplex GRPO) at PoC scale.
- #565 / #858 — simplex OPD, landed; shared adapter/foundation.
- #566 — streaming duplex OPD; out of scope here, reuses the trajectory contract from this work.
- #700 — roadmap item "MiniCPM-o, streaming & duplex RL".
- #723 — layered reward scorer interface; reward scorers here align with its direction.

## 9. References

- MiniCPM-o 4.5 technical report: arXiv 2604.27393; model and code: https://github.com/OpenBMB/MiniCPM-V , https://huggingface.co/openbmb/MiniCPM-o-4_5
- vLLM-Omni MiniCPM-o 4.5 duplex runtime: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/3907
- Kyutai multi-faceted interactivity alignment (replay-based event-sliced GRPO): arXiv 2606.11167; aligned checkpoints: https://huggingface.co/kyutai (moshika-rl-seamless, personaplex-rl-seamless)
- GRPO: arXiv 2402.03300
- ASPIRin (raw-token collapse and action-space projection): arXiv 2604.10065

raw.title: [AI COLLABORATION HUB] Shared task claims, ownership and handoffs
raw.body:
# FRIDAY Universe — Shared AI Collaboration Hub

This issue is the persistent, shared claim and handoff thread for every AI and human collaborator working in FRIDAY Universe.

## Authority and scope
- `docs/MASTER_PLAN.md` remains the source of project objectives, dependencies and acceptance criteria.
- `docs/collaboration/WORK_BOARD.yaml` is the operational mirror of task ownership and progress.
- `docs/collaboration/FILE_OWNERSHIP.yaml` records protected file/component claims.
- This issue is the externally visible coordination thread for claims, releases, blockers and handoffs. It is not a competing roadmap.

## Claim protocol
Before editing a task's files, post one top-level comment in this issue with:

```text
CLAIM TASK-ID
Collaborator: <registered collaborator ID>
Branch: <branch name>
PR: <number or none>
Files: <paths or components>
Started: <UTC ISO-8601>
Expected next update: <UTC ISO-8601>
```

A claim is active only after the branch and file list are recorded in the shared work board. Check for an existing active claim and overlapping file ownership first. Do not begin overlapping work while a claim is active unless the owner explicitly agrees in this thread.

For simultaneous claims, pause both edits and resolve ownership in this thread; do not assume that a local branch update constitutes a lock.

## Release / handoff protocol
Post:
- `RELEASE TASK-ID` when work is handed off or abandoned.
- `HANDOFF TASK-ID` with completed work, test evidence, branch/PR, blockers and the exact next action.
- `BLOCKED TASK-ID` with the dependency and who can unblock it.
- `REVIEW TASK-ID PR-NUMBER` with reproducible findings.

Claims must be renewed with a status update when the expected update time passes. A missing update does not authorize another collaborator to overwrite work; first contact the owner and preserve the branch.

## Safety
No force-pushes, blind resets, unapproved merges, production changes, secret disclosure or destructive operations. The project owner retains final approval for merges and deployments.

All collaborators — Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, ZAI, Vercel v0 and future contributors — are equal participants. Register actual tool/access capabilities; do not assume capabilities from a product name.

raw.title: fix(ui): place all banner ads above screen content across Android flavors
raw.body:
## User-facing problem
Banner advertisements appear **below the content or near the bottom navigation** in some of the 17 Android flavors, while other screens already show them near the top. The inconsistent placement makes the applications feel different and can displace the bottom navigation or primary controls.

## Expected behavior
- Every **banner ad placement** appears at the **top of its screen's content**, directly below the screen/header area and above the main list, reader, compass, counter or audio controls.
- Preserve normal bottom navigation (no banner anchored above/below it) and useful first-screen content, including short/landscape viewports, consent changes and Premium/ad-free users.
- Keep native feed ads as native feed placements; do not create unexpected **banner** fallbacks deep in the feed.
- Retain consent, subscription gating, existing ad unit IDs, ad sizes, and ad load/retry protections; do not add extra banner requests or multiple banner slots per screen.
- Apply consistently across all supported flavors and secondary screens: prayer schedules/location picker, Qibla, Zikir counter, prayer/Esma/Mucize lists, content detail, Qur'an lists/detail/bookmarks, settings and relevant routes.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Map all banner call sites; remove/move bottom-of-screen banner placements into predictable top slots.
- [ ] Automated UI/structural tests prevent regression, especially on compact/landscape screens and for native fallback.
- [ ] Run repository tests and CI, then verify physical Android screen placement for representative installed Play-signed builds **after the fix is packaged**. Existing installed Internal builds do not prove new changes.
- [ ] No unrelated navigation, telemetry, billing or release-policy changes.
- [ ] One cohesive PR; Mergify/required checks remain sole merge gate. Production promotions remain independent of this issue.

Related to #998 (reader/nav acceptance) and #372 (ads optimization).

Каждый чат сверяет свежие PR/CI/runtime непосредственно перед действиями.

## 0. УТОЧНЁННОЕ РЕШЕНИЕ ВЛАДЕЛЬЦА — 16.11.2026: ПРИЁМКА И CODEX

**Фактическую приёмку проводит только владелец лично** (локальный UI, Симулятор, PAPER, VPS). CI, тесты и технические receipts — доказательства для анализа, но не подмена личной приёмки. Статус `ACCEPTED` — только после явного подтверждения владельца.

**Запрещено передавать Codex интерактивное управление компьютером владельца:** курсор, мышь, клики, GUI-кнопки, ввод в окна и дистанционное управление рабочим столом. **Это не запрет терминальной работы Codex:** исключительные задачи и синхронизация с VPS допускаются в ранее действовавших границах и по конкретному поручению владельца, без GUI-управления. Никаких автоматических расширений доступа к файлам/сервисам или торговых полномочий.

**Все направления ANALYSIS / SCANNER_ROBOT / MONOLITH:** код и CI — через GitHub; для реальной UI/локальной приёмки готовить минимальные шаги владельцу, не имитировать действия курсором. Ранее данное мной широкое толкование «Codex вообще без доступа к компьютеру / запрещён локальный терминал» **отменено как ошибочное**. Незавершённый VPS preflight остаётся `UNPROVEN`, без автоматического повторения; защищённые merge/deploy/STOP/START/PAPER/LIVE разрешения действуют отдельно.

## 1. РЕШЕНИЕ ПО САМООПРЕДЕЛЕНИЮ ЧАТОВ

| Существующий чат | Постоянное название / роль | Точный статус и следующий шаг |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **«Локальная Машина времени»** | **ROLE_CONFIRMED → «Анализ сделок и Симулятор»** (`ANALYSIS`). Единственный владелец Diary/Statistics/OriginalEpisodeSignalChart/Replay, локального historical data, exact-ID связи. Принимает незавершённую production/UI приёмку #1070/#1072/#1074. | **A1:** [PR #1076](https://github.com/svobodaXXI/BybitScanner/pull/1076) **MERGED**, stable `fbf999b0750deb9d560fe8989e099e60ad54eae9`; ноутбучная установка и пользовательская приёмка **PENDING**. Самостоятельно продолжать read-only exact-ID baseline и согласовать безопасную локальную приёмку; не трогать trading runtime. [Предложение роли](https://github.com/svobodaXXI/BybitScanner/issues/1077#issuecomment-6903023082). |
| **«Статистика и графики сделок»** | **READY_FOR_ARCHIVE / ROLE_NOT_ASSIGNED**. Исходная приёмка #1074 передана `ANALYSIS`; прежние #508 Horn CLAIM и назначение Scanner/Robot **отозваны**. | Никаких новых PR/задач; владелец может архивировать. [Ответ](https://github.com/svobodaXXI/BybitScanner/issues/1077#issuecomment-6903021845). |
| **«Интерфейс Статистики»** | **READY_FOR_ARCHIVE / ROLE_NOT_ASSIGNED**. #1070/#1072 merged; непринятая production UI проверка передана `ANALYSIS`. | Никаких новых PR/задач; владелец может архивировать. [HANDOFF](https://github.com/svobodaXXI/BybitScanner/issues/1077#issuecomment-6901794820). |
| **Новый чат «Scanner и Robot»** | **ROLE_CONFIRMED → «Scanner и Robot»** (`SCANNER_ROBOT`). Единственный ответственный за торговый Scanner/Robot core, detector geometry, входы, STOP/безубыток, L2/поток ордеров; не владеет Diary/Replay или VPS monolith. [Регистрация](https://github.com/svobodaXXI/BybitScanner/issues/1077#issuecomment-6903102442). | **S0:** уже ведёт read-only сверку первоочередного доказанного Robot/Scanner дефекта и owning gate; затем заявляет один узкий CLAIM перед изменением кода. Сохраняет Draft PR #1024 без спекулятивного слияния; никаких trading/deploy mutations без разрешения. |
| **Этот координационный чат** | **ROLE_CONFIRMED → «Монолит и релизы»** (`MONOLITH`). Единственный владелец Windows VPS Manager, SSH/устройств, монолитных релизов/receipts и межтрековой совместимости. | **M1:** read-only подтверждение installed/stable/PR/CI и подготовка единого безопасного релизного пути. Никакого VPS UPDATE/STOP/START/PAPER mutation без применимого разрешения владельца. |

**Все три направления назначены:** `ANALYSIS`, `SCANNER_ROBOT`, `MONOLITH`. Прежний профильный чат Mirror/Robot архивирован; новый «Scanner и Robot» зарегистрирован. Реальная готовность PR/релиза/торговли проверяется отдельно. Цель — **ровно три активных чата** (`ANALYSIS`, `SCANNER_ROBOT`, `MONOLITH`), существующие чаты переименовывает владелец после ROLE_CONFIRMED. Передачи приняты, #1076 **MERGED**, но локальная ноутбучная приёмка #1076 и реальная UI-приёмка #1072/#1074 **PENDING**. Слияние и установка всегда имеют отдельные разрешения.

## 2. ПЯТИСТРОЧНАЯ ПЛАНЁРКА — БЕЗ ПЕРЕСЫЛКИ ЛОГОВ ВЛАДЕЛЬЦЕМ

**На каждом новом рабочем заходе:** открой эту доску → последние релевантные комментарии → свой PR/owning spec → если задача свободна, начинай свою строку; **не жди нового персонального промпта**, когда дальнейшее действие является безопасной read-only проверкой или разработкой через PR.

Пиши комментарий **только на границе** (CLAIM, PR READY, зависимость, merge, deploy verified, handoff). Формат:

```text
CHAT=<текущее имя> | TRACK=ANALYSIS/SCANNER_ROBOT/MONOLITH
TASK=<один результат и PR/issue> | STATE=CLAIMED/IN_PROGRESS/CODE_READY/MERGE_AUTH_REQUIRED/MERGED/DEPLOY_AUTH_REQUIRED/ACCEPTANCE_PENDING/ACCEPTED/BLOCKED
FILES=<пути или API> | EVIDENCE=<текущий SHA, CI, receipt; только факты>
NEXT=<что делает сам чат / какая конкретная зависимость>
```

**Перед правкой** сравни `FILES` с другими CLAIM и фактическими PR diff. При конфликте `CONFLICT`: уступи единственному владельцу файла; договорись о последовательности здесь, а не одновременно меняй код. Получателю передавать `HANDOFF`, подтверждать `HANDOFF_ACCEPTED`. Если ждать merge/deploy разрешения, можно вести **только независимый** подготовительный пункт из своей очереди, не маскируя блокировку и не затрагивая конфликтные файлы.

## 3. КАК ПОНИМАТЬ ГОТОВНОСТЬ

- `CODE_READY`: актуальный PR HEAD, обязательные CI success, проверенные conflict/scope. **Не разрешает merge.**
- `MERGED`: GitHub merge и включение commit в нужный stable. **Не означает релиз.**
- `DEPLOYED_VERIFIED`: exact installed SHA, protected receipts, проверка runtime/API. Нельзя выводить из GitHub CI, SSH_OK или systemd status.
- `ACCEPTED`: реальная UI/replay/PAPER-проверка; отдельно от CI/деплоя.
- Owner approval обязателен для merge/host mutations/STOP/START/PAPER admission по действующим контрактам. **PAPER only, LIVE запрещён**; защита STOP/TAKE и DB identity остаётся fail-closed.

**Ограничение связи:** ChatGPT-чаты не получают мгновенные GitHub push-уведомления и не работают в фоне только из-за комментария здесь. Каждый чат **сам читает** эту доску при следующем обращении; никаких обещаний, что другой чат узнает об изменении, пока он не активирован.

**Продуктовый цикл:** убыточная фактическая сделка → Статистика → точный replay → обоснованное изменение Scanner/Robot → независимый holdout → разрешённая PAPER-проверка net P&L/риска. Второстепенные функции — в backlog.

raw.title: Product: mature-campaign gameplay and world-changing Legacy victories
raw.body:
## Scope update — 2026-10-10

At the requester's explicit direction, this issue now tracks the broader product design for **mature-campaign gameplay and world-changing Legacy victories**. The discussion deliberately expanded beyond the original AI verification/runtime investigation. The former exclusion of gameplay, AI personality, presentation, diplomacy, and content is superseded for this product-planning scope.

The original runtime investigation is preserved below as a distinct workstream and historical record. Its measurements and code references need fresh verification. Richer gameplay does not demonstrate better performance, and this scope change does not authorize weaker verification, reduced simulation coverage, approximate rules, or timeout-only fixes.

## Product objective

Make a developed civilization enjoyable to inhabit and direct across long campaigns. Players should have consequential choices, discoveries, cooperation, rivalry, memorable places, and visible accomplishments—not merely occupied production queues or repeated administrative work.

Support the full range of interests: **builder/caretaker, merchant, diplomat, scholar, explorer/collector, cultural patron and schools of thought, spiritual leader, conqueror/tactician, and protector/liberator**. Interests and undertakings can overlap; they are not nine mandatory checklists or mutually exclusive victory selections.

Fun, excitement, gameplay, and attachment to the civilization are the leading criteria. Existing games inform the design, but paper comparisons are not evidence of Conquestoria's balance or enjoyment.

## Accepted direction

- **Legacy scale:** a finale must establish a world-changing achievement with substantial realized consequences and meaningful variety. A few tiles, demonstrations, shipments, ceremonies, or buildings are insufficient. The framework defines how achievements qualify; it does not prescribe one ideology, technology, or landmark.
- **Progression and payoff:** discoveries and undertakings produce useful capabilities and visible changes before victory. Applied science follows discovery, application, and transformation. Natural development should ordinarily span multiple eras; there is no arbitrary era floor, generic future-tech ladder, final ceremony project, or extra countdown.
- **Flexible ambition:** multiple pursuits can coexist. Real capabilities and commitments create opportunity costs. Advisors help identify opportunities; routine operation proceeds automatically within authorized commitments.
- **Solo and cooperation:** independent players remain competitive and can trade or cooperate without sharing victory. Genuine shared victory requires an explicit undertaking and substantial fulfilled complementary roles. Qualified co-winners have equal standing, with protection against expulsion erasing earned contributions.
- **Cultural breadth and agency:** culture includes art, philosophy, schools of thought, civic and spiritual traditions, and collective as well as individual priorities. No universal Western political ideal or single government form defines success. Current cultural candidates require consequential foreign practice; a strictly isolated cultural finale is parked as unproven.
- **Cultural attribution:** local adaptation and independence do not automatically erase foundational contributions. Several contributors can matter without dividing a fixed ownership percentage. Historical ancestry alone does not confer unlimited qualifying reach. Actual affected scope counts once within each claim, and shared eligibility remains separate.
- **Purposeful transformation:** engineering, ecological recovery, and combinations are viable directions. Transformation can be proactive and aspirational; it need not repair a manufactured crisis. Large intentional changes and relocation can have real benefits, opposition, costs, and consequences.
- **Knowledge and security:** most knowledge diffuses gradually; advanced knowledge may remain unusable without prerequisites. Standing secrecy/sharing choices replace per-discovery administration. Theft and sabotage can affect knowledge, specialized equipment, capabilities, and real operation. Provenance and historical credit persist.
- **Competition and endings:** Legacy coexists with existing domination. The first qualifying competitive result ends the race; optional continued play preserves the world and records later accomplishments. Independent Legacy claims qualifying at the earliest common end-of-world-turn checkpoint can win simultaneously. Domination/elimination interactions still need precise resolution.
- **AI:** values, personality, circumstances, commitments, and earned information shape genuine pursuit, proposals, cooperation, refusal, and obstruction. Difficulty improves execution without omniscience or a universal anti-player coalition.
- **Fair setbacks:** rivalry and refusal of new work do not erase functioning foreign practice. Actual loss of a required function can obstruct unfinished qualification. Solo opportunities should be credible across varied ordinary campaigns, without guaranteeing every candidate a finish from every position.
- **Redirection and identity:** changing ambitions does not cancel promises, spend resources, or erase achievements. Reassigning real capacity carries real costs and consequences. Earlier choices can enable new capabilities; results should visibly and functionally change ordinary play; further applications should create meaningfully different decisions. Useful partial achievements do not become consolation victories.

Cultural city acquisition, including exceptional capital/final-city loss, is accepted in principle only with the agreed extreme conditions, clear warnings, and meaningful recovery. Exact conditions remain unresolved; cultural Legacy does not require annexation.

## Current state

| Area | State |
|---|---|
| Core experience and shared principles | Largely settled |
| Culture | Deeply explored; consolidate accepted rules and close exact scope/qualification questions |
| Applied science and engineering/ecology | Strong direction and substantial examples; exact qualifying packages remain open |
| Commerce, diplomacy, exploration, spirituality, protection, military Legacy | Earlier candidates exist; need stronger distinct gameplay and world-changing culmination benchmarks |
| Winner-determining edge cases | Still require closure |
| Numerical balance, opportunity frequency, AI competence, pacing, player enjoyment | Not validated; require later prototype/playtest evidence |
| Implementation | No gameplay implementation or implementation-ready specification produced by this planning discussion |

Recent accepted examples show cultural teaching institutions enabling a separately developed coastal-recovery application. Their point is continuity of capability and visible results—not automatic transfer of victory progress, guaranteed recovery, or approval of every illustrative ecological effect.

## Remaining product-planning work

Working estimate: **about five substantial review passes**, potentially several exchanges each, assuming the portfolio remains stable. This is not a delivery date, percentage-complete claim, or implementation estimate.

- [ ] **Portfolio:** establish distinct playable benchmarks across all nine interests: consequential choices, useful intermediate results, a convincing finale, a useful near miss, and appropriate independent/shared possibilities.
- [ ] **Qualification:** resolve actual affected scope, world reference, relevant variety, overlaps, populations/borders, shared versus independent accounting, fundamental discovery, and supported domestic routes. Trial tuning values must be labeled as such.
- [ ] **Ending and eligibility:** resolve domination versus Legacy ordering, elimination, succession, and remaining contribution/breach cases that can change the winner.
- [ ] **Whole-campaign experience:** compare ordinary/advanced starts, solo/shared play, civilization sizes, AI pursuit, mature-city standing work, advisory attention, setbacks, and continued play.
- [ ] **Consolidation and sign-off:** produce one concise product brief separating accepted rules, candidate benchmarks, prototype parameters, parked ideas, and validation questions.

Next focus: the portfolio pass, beginning with commercial and diplomatic accomplishments. New proposals remain candidates until reviewed.

## Product-planning definition of done

The intended experience is coherent across the full portfolio; concrete benchmarks explain actions and changed outcomes; there are no known unresolved contradictions in winner-determining rules; player/AI information and commitment boundaries are clear; and remaining uncertainties have explicit prototype or implementation follow-up.

Do not continue expanding examples solely because more can be written. Prices, durations, threshold tuning, opportunity frequency, attention burden, and enjoyment need empirical validation. Implementation architecture, save representation, authoritative gameplay/UI wiring, deterministic tests, and performance planning come afterward with a fresh scoped repository review.

---

<details>
<summary>Original runtime investigation — historical description and separate verification concerns</summary>

The following text is preserved from the original issue. Its runtime-only scope and gameplay exclusions are superseded by the scope update above. Measurements and statements about “current” code reflect the original investigation, not a fresh October 10 verification. Behavior-preserving optimization criteria apply to that runtime workstream, not as a prohibition on separately approved gameplay changes.

## Summary

`yarn test:ai-long`'s full 9-scenario long-horizon matrix is the project's strongest cross-system defect-discovery mechanism (it has caught expansion stalls, worker-demand deletion, save/reload determinism drift, and consolidation-retention bugs that no short test caught). Its checked-in runtime story has drifted badly enough that it can no longer reliably serve as a practical pre-merge gate:

- `.claude/rules/ai-simulation.md` still says the matrix "costs ~20 minutes" and to "Keep the whole matrix under ~25 minutes."
- `tests/simulation/long-horizon/campaign-scenarios.ts`'s own header now documents the matrix at "≈ 40 min as of #1094's AI gold-spending pass" (sequential sum of its own per-row comments is ≈ 37.3 min, consistent).
- `lh-veteran-large` (the matrix's largest scenario) is documented at **1520s**, up from **427.8s pre-#1094** — a genuine ~3.5x increase attributed almost entirely to `#1094`'s AI rush-buy path (`src/ai/ai-treasury.ts` → `getRushBuyQuote` → `calculateCivEconomy`).
- In response, `6bbe6e67` ("perf(ai): attribute and bound #1094's gold-spending cost on lh-veteran-large") cached only the *maintenance* recomputation across cities in one round, explicitly left `calculateCivEconomy`'s cost "out of scope to restructure," and **tripled `SCENARIO_TIMEOUT_MS` from 1,500,000ms to 4,800,000ms** — a timeout-only band-aid on the actual redundant-work problem.
- `scripts/run-ai-long-horizon.sh`'s outer wrapper timeout is still hardcoded to 3600s (60 min) — now *smaller* than the new 4,800,000ms (80 min) per-scenario Vitest timeout, so a legitimately slow worst-case run would be killed by the outer wrapper before the inner timeout ever mattered, turning a real regression signal into an ambiguous "wrapper timeout."
- `tests/simulation/long-horizon/known-campaign-gaps.ts` currently has two live entries (`expansion-frozen` for `lh-veteran-medium`, and `production-idle` scoped `'any'`) pointing at **issue #1066**, which was closed today (2026-09-18, commit `871f64a`) by the auto-explore multi-hop lookahead fix. Per the register's own two-way-ratchet contract, this state needs reconciliation (verify whether the findings still reproduce, and if so re-point them to a live owner; delete if fixed).

## Root-cause lead to investigate (not yet proven as the *sole* cause)

Code read against current `main` (`be6d2322`) shows `applyAIGoldSpending` (`src/ai/ai-treasury.ts`) calls `getRushBuyQuote` once per actively-producing city, and `getRushBuyQuote` (`src/systems/economy-system.ts:690`) unconditionally calls `calculateCivEconomy`, which calls `projectCivGrossGold` **twice** (base + pirate-modified) and `calculateMaintenance` once. `projectCivGrossGold` itself iterates every city in the civ (`calculateProjectedCityYields`, wonder bonuses) and calls `getCitiesConnectedToCapital`, a BFS over the map's road network — all **per call**. A successful purchase inside `rushBuyActiveProduction` re-invokes `getRushBuyQuote` a second time on unchanged state (a provably exact redundancy, not just a suspected one). Net shape: roughly `O(producing_cities × cities)` whole-civ economy re-projection per AI civ per round — worse as `#1064`'s expansion fix lets civs legitimately grow to more cities over a campaign, which lines up with the late-round cost growth the issue needs to characterize.

This is a **falsifiable lead**, not a decision. It must be measured (call counts, wall time share, growth shape) before being treated as the fix target, per the investigation this issue scopes.

## Scope

This is a **stability/runtime infrastructure** issue only:

- Restore `yarn test:ai-long` to a practical, trustworthy pre-merge gate (target: the project's historical ≤25-minute intent, or documented evidence for why that's currently impossible).
- Eliminate exact redundant computation — same behavior, same coverage, same scenario matrix, same invariant battery, materially less duplicated work.
- Add a machine-independent deterministic work-budget guard around the actual regression class (extending `tests/perf/algorithmic-budgets.test.ts`'s existing pattern), not just a wall-clock number.
- Reconcile `known-campaign-gaps.ts`'s stale `#1066` references against a fresh full-matrix run.

Explicitly **out of scope**: AI competence/personality/national-intent/presentation/diplomacy/content work, reducing scenario turns/maps/AI counts, weakening detectors or invariants, approximating economy/combat/production rules, or any fix that is "increase the timeout and stop."

## Definition of done

- Fresh full-matrix run completes and is measured (per-scenario timing, growth curves, worst-case reproduction).
- Deterministic operation counts (not just wall clock) identify the dominant redundant-work source(s); the `#1094`/`getRushBuyQuote` hypothesis above is confirmed, refined, or disproven with evidence.
- The smallest correct fix is implemented via TDD: exact reuse/precomputation at the right orchestration boundary, not caching with fuzzy invalidation, not an AI-only legality shortcut (human and AI rush-buy must stay on one canonical legality path).
- Campaign artifacts are byte-identical before/after unless a change is an intentionally justified correctness fix.
- `known-campaign-gaps.ts`'s stale `#1066` entries are reconciled (deleted if fixed, re-pointed to a live owner if not).
- `.claude/rules/ai-simulation.md`, `campaign-scenarios.ts`'s header comment, and the outer wrapper/timeout layers are brought back into agreement with reality.
- A deterministic performance-budget regression exists so this class of drift is caught mechanically going forward, not rediscovered by another timeout bump.


</details>

raw.title: Investigate production AdMob no-fill vs technical failures and UMP consent errors
raw.body:
## Live measurements (1–15 October 2026, Google accounts accessed read-only via Ops)

**AdMob (publisher account in TRY):** 104,895 requests, 92,119 matched requests, 18,141 impressions, 654 clicks, estimated ₺776.93. Match rate ≈87.8%; impressions/matched ≈19.7% (not a technical error rate: includes preloads, pacing and unshown ads). All 17 framework AdMob App IDs match LIVE APPROVED records. Other 4 unlinked historical AdMob apps are ACTION_REQUIRED; do not infer these block the 17 current framework apps.

**GA4 Firebase property:** 95,106 ad_request_sent, **63,054 ad_failed_to_load**, 69,918 ad_suppressed, **10,536 consent_error** and 11,012 consent_flow_started. These are **event counts, not unique-user failure rates** and not directly comparable to AdMob API requests.

**Ad load failures by format in GA4:** native 22,461; app_open 14,294; banner 13,820; interstitial 12,348; rewarded 91; rewarded_interstitial 40. Largest affected framework stream: com.parsfilo.namazsurelerivedualarsesli (18,471 ad_failed_to_load, 2,296 consent_error, 20,784 ad_request_sent, 1,662 consent_flow_started). Multiple consent_error events can occur per consent attempt/session; do not divide these counts into a user failure percentage.

**Diagnostic gap verified:** GA4 report dimension customEvent:ad_format works; customEvent:consent_trigger, customEvent:suppress_reason and customEvent:error_code are not registered/available via Data API. Android AdRevenueLogger.logFailedToLoad emits numeric errorCode (including SDK code 3, normal NO_FILL), so the GA4 ad_failed_to_load total currently **cannot distinguish normal no-fill from technical faults**. Repo runtime-observability-policy.json correctly instructs excluding no-fill code 3 from the technical failure rate, but live report lacks the breakdown needed to apply this criterion.

## Focused acceptance criteria

- Attribute sample ad failures by SDK error domain/code (exclude no-fill code 3) and by format, app flavor, released app version and placement; do not log tokens, raw responses or personally identifying values.
- Distinguish UMP information-update / form-load / refresh errors by sanitized error category; check user-facing consent behavior without bypassing permissions and without treating all errors as policy failures.
- Validate two high-signal app samples on an actual device: Namaz Sureleri Sesli and İsmi Azam Duası, then verify representative AdMob/GA4 events against live AdMob counts in equal time zones and date ranges.
- Investigate excessive app_open and native preload-to-show gaps without optimizing for the wrong KPI; separate legitimate pacing/consent suppression from true serving failures.
- Use Play Vitals and Crashlytics release-specific diagnostics; don't roll out new Android releases until measured technical failures and UMP are bounded.
- Keep changes proportional: no billing enablement, weakening consent requirements, mass SDK refactor, or repeated re-release of 17 flavors for non-causal guesses.

## Other separately tracked findings

Firestore 50K/day no-cost read quota exceeded; indexed overview and coverage optimized in PRs #332/#334. Admin UI false release-drift and unknown-as-zero issues addressed in PR #336; those are **not** the cause of UMP/revenue events.

Source revision assessed: main 72eab1b3c74c002254c2904c92ce45926cb4e403.

labels.name: agent-working

raw.body:
The multi-seed fix (#1137, `d4b66cf`) stopped pairing seed 0's artifact with pooled scores, and its note now says the pooled numbers "describe the method, not a single artifact". The same report's `next` field still tells the reader to ship one: on a two-seed run whose artifacts differ and whose pooled evidence promotes, `run.artifact_hash` and `run.reported_seed` are `None` while `next` is "review the artifact diff" / "apply it as a separate, explicit step". So the card refuses to name an artifact in four places and then instructs the user to review and apply it — the pairing the fix removed from the run block is still in the advice the user acts on.

Repro at `d4b66cf`, offline, no key and no model call (a stub `evolve` returns a different artifact per seed, both of which cover the test rules):

```bash
PYTHONPATH=$PWD python3 - <<'PY'
from tests import test_pilot as T
import agentdescent.pilot as P
from agentdescent.pilot import pilot

def fake_evolve(*a, **k):
    seed = k.get("seed", 0)
    text = "R0 R1 R2" if seed == 0 else "R0 R1 R2 plus seed1"
    return T._StubResult(rendered=text, final_reward=0.9)

P.evolve = fake_evolve
rep = pilot(T._policy(), T._config(seeds=(0, 1)))
print(rep.action, rep.run["artifact_hash"], rep.run["reported_seed"])
print(list(rep.next))
PY
```

Output:

```
promote None None
['review the artifact diff', 'apply it as a separate, explicit step', 'keep the manifest and this report for audit']
```

With the stub from `tests/test_pilot.py::test_pooled_scores_are_not_paired_with_the_first_seed_artifact` (seed 0 artifact empty, seed 1 `"R0 R1 R2"`) the action is `reject`, so the contradiction only shows when both seeds produce a *different but equally good* artifact — exactly the case the new note describes.

Checked the 23 open issues (1120, 1113, 1112, 1111, 1098, 1094, 1092, 1091, 1082, 998, 965, 964, 963, 951, 948, 942, 941, 937, 921, 221, 150, 76, 52); #937 is the parent feature issue and its remaining slice is the CLI/docs page, not this line.

Add:

- pass the per-seed agreement into the PROMOTE branch of `_next_actions` (`agentdescent/pilot.py:410-422`, both call sites `:672` and `:689`) so that when `artifacts_agree` is false the steps name the artifacts that exist — e.g. "pick one seed's artifact from `run.per_seed` and review that diff", "apply the chosen artifact as a separate, explicit step", keeping the manifest line — instead of "review the artifact diff" / "apply it".
- one row in `tests/test_pilot.py` on the existing stubbed-evolve shape: artifacts differ and the pooled evidence promotes → `report.action == "promote"`, `run.artifact_hash is None`, and no step contains "review the artifact diff" or "apply it"; the agreeing two-seed and single-seed reports keep today's text.
- one `Fixed` changelog fragment.

Acceptance: a promoting two-seed report whose artifacts differ has `next` naming the per-seed artifacts and never "review the artifact diff"/"apply it", while the single-seed and agreeing-seed reports keep their current `next`; a test row fails on `d4b66cf` and passes with the change.

Non-goals: the pooled interval and the promote/defer policy, the `run.per_seed` shape, the CLI verb and `docs/pilot.md` (#937 step 3), and the silent `reflect=agent` default (#1137 item 4).

**In this slice (design §7, §14 row 6):**
- **`clue_to`:** from a clue entry to its mystery thread, marked "points to it" or "false lead". It's a DM-only mark: the readers never mark a false lead.
- **Readers suggest clues and who found them:**
  - the lore reader suggests a clue tied to a mystery it already reads;
  - the session reader suggests a clue the party found, with who found it (the knower lists, as today).

  Both are suggestions the DM keeps or turns down, never added by themselves. Consent and the session-reader rules are as in slice 5: speakers and line starts kept, the sweep, and one change with one Undo.
- **"Solved so far":** worked out when shown, never stored, in the four forms of §7's table. A fraction appears only when the DM tied a list. DMbot never invents a total and never says a guess is right or wrong.
- **Players:** a player sees only the clues their own characters know, never a total (§10). A clue only some people know keeps `audience_limited`, and the #4524 guard applies to every clue write.
- **The website half:** filed as its own issue for WebDev when this one's design is ruled (#3663).

- storage (whether `clue_to` is a connection kind or a column, and any migration);

raw.body:
#129 / #167 hoisted the *report* inputs above `ev.mkdir` in all four record
writers, and #168 / PR #171 finished the job for `make_controls_record.py`'s
`--base-record` and `--job-log`. One class of input is still read after the
evidence `.json.gz` files are on disk in all three *other* writers: a
repo-tracked constant, not an argv path.

This was explicitly **out of scope** for #168 (the Curator's "Out of Scope"
section names `make_record.py` and `make_column_record.py`), so it is filed
here rather than held against PR #171.

## Observed

Measured on `origin/main` @ `2fa184c`. `make_record.py` invoked with every
report input present and parseable, and only `design/bitcell/sizing.json`
replaced with `{` (truncated JSON); provenance subprocess stubbed, same shape
as the suite's `RefusesBeforeWritingEvidence.stub_provenance`, plus the
suite's own `snm_from_artifacts` module stub:

```
raised: JSONDecodeError Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 1 column 2 (char 1)
gzips left: ['hold_snm_corners.report.json.gz', 'mc_read_snm.report0.json.gz',
             'read_snm_corners.report.json.gz', 'write_trip_corners.report.json.gz']
```

Four orphaned `.json.gz` files in the evidence directory the published record
cites — the exact outcome #129's acceptance criteria make impossible for the
report inputs. The read is `make_record.py:99`
(`sizing = json.load(open(repo / "design/bitcell/sizing.json"))`); `ev.mkdir`
is at `:89` and the four `save_gz_json` calls at `:90-91`.

## Same shape, structurally identical, NOT separately measured

These two were read from the source, not exercised — no probe was run against
either, so treat the orphaning as expected-by-construction rather than
demonstrated:

- `make_write_mc_record.py:128` — the identical
  `sizing = json.load(open(repo / "design/bitcell/sizing.json"))`, with
  `ev.mkdir` at `:76` and the gzip writes at `:77-78`.
- `make_column_record.py:167` — `sha(repo / f'sim/column/requests/{b}.request.json')`
  (`read_bytes()`, defined at `:152`), with `ev.mkdir` at `:148` and the gzip
  writes at `:150`.

`make_controls_record.py` reads no such constant, so it is already complete
after PR #171 — its hoisted-block comment was correctly narrowed to "Every
**report** input" there.

## Severity (lower than #168, deliberately)

`design/bitcell/sizing.json` and `sim/column/requests/*.request.json` are
repo-tracked files, always present in a checkout — unlike `--base-record`,
which is an argv path a caller can get wrong. The reachable trigger is a
local edit that leaves one of them unparseable (or a partial checkout), not a
mistyped command line. That is a real but narrower window, which is why this
is filed as a suggestion rather than as a defect against #171.

## Suggested fix (and its real cost)

Hoist the three reads above their `ev.mkdir` and extend
`RefusesBeforeWritingEvidence` with an unparseable-`sizing.json` case per
writer. The cost is not the diff: all three files are attested members of
`sim/testbench-inventory.json`, so editing them drags the full item-9
re-attestation cascade (cold-start `sim/run_all_benches.sh`,
`evidence/item9.json`, `klt signoff --check`).

Per #129's own severity note and the disposition #168 adopted: **ride the next
PR that already owes the item-9 cascade** rather than paying it for this
alone. Note that PR #171 paid that cascade for #168 on its own anyway, so a
carrier is not guaranteed to appear — if none does within a few cycles,
landing this on its own is a defensible call.

A measured refutation closes this issue completely: if someone instruments
these three paths and finds the reads cannot in fact orphan evidence (e.g. a
guard upstream that this review missed), closing with that evidence fully
discharges it.

Discovered while evaluating PR #171 (issue #168).

[loom dashboard](https://dashboard.2amlogic.com/github.com/2AMLogic/sky130-sram-compiler/issues/172)

---

## Curator Enhancement (2026-11-17, against `origin/main` @ `afa3b36`)

### Verified corrections

- **2026-11-17, verified against `origin/main` @ `afa3b36`** (`git show origin/main:<path> | grep -nE 'ev\.mkdir|save_gz_json|sizing\.json'`): the three line citations in the body hold. `sim/bitcell/lib/make_record.py`: `ev.mkdir` `:89`, `save_gz_json` `:91`, `sizing = json.load(open(repo / "design/bitcell/sizing.json"))` `:99`. `sim/bitcell/lib/make_write_mc_record.py`: `ev.mkdir` `:76`, gzip write `:78`, sizing read `:128`. `sim/column/lib/make_column_record.py`: `ev.mkdir` `:148`, gzip write `:150`, `sha()` defined `:152`, called at `:167`. Read from source only; no probe run by the Curator, and the `make_record.py` measurement in the body is the filer's.
- Paths: the body's bare filenames live under `sim/bitcell/lib/` (first two) and `sim/column/lib/` (third). All three are in `sim/testbench-inventory.json` (lines 73, 75, 38 at `afa3b36`).
- Main moved since the body's `2fa184c` (PR #171 merged); it touched only `make_controls_record.py` and the test file's hoist cases, so no citation above shifted.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] In each of `make_record.py`, `make_write_mc_record.py`, `make_column_record.py`, the repo-tracked constant read (`sizing.json`; per-bench `sim/column/requests/{b}.request.json` sha) happens before `ev.mkdir`, alongside the existing hoisted report inputs, with the comment above the hoisted block updated to say "every input, report and repo-tracked constant".
- [ ] `RefusesBeforeWritingEvidence` (`sim/bitcell/lib/test_record_common.py`) gains one case per writer: an unparseable `sizing.json` (column: an unreadable request file) makes `main()` raise and leave zero `.json.gz` in the evidence dir, using the existing `assert_refused` helper. Each new case fails on the pre-change code (confirm by running it against `afa3b36`'s writers and quoting the failing output in the PR).
- [ ] Item-9 re-attestation cascade done once for all three files (`sim/run_all_benches.sh` cold start, `evidence/item9.json`, `klt signoff --check`).

### Implementation Guidance
Hoist, don't guard: move the three reads above `ev.mkdir`, mirroring how #129/#168 hoisted report inputs. For the column writer, compute the per-bench request shas into a dict before `ev.mkdir` and use it at `:167`. Rejected: wrapping the writes in a temp-dir-then-rename (new mechanism for a 3-line move); a shared `read_inputs()` helper (premature for three call sites).

Carrier note: all three are attested inventory members, so this pays the full cascade. Per the body, land it with the next PR that owes the cascade; a Builder picking it up standalone is defensible but should say so in the PR. Per the body, a measured refutation (an upstream guard that makes the orphaning unreachable) closes the issue.

### Out of Scope
- `make_controls_record.py` (reads no such constant; already complete after #171).
- Report-input ordering (done in #129/#167/#168), `git_short_sha` cleanliness (#151), any change to record content.
- Making evidence writes atomic in general.

### Affected Files
- `sim/bitcell/lib/make_record.py` - hoist sizing read above `ev.mkdir`
- `sim/bitcell/lib/make_write_mc_record.py` - same
- `sim/column/lib/make_column_record.py` - precompute request shas before `ev.mkdir`
- `sim/bitcell/lib/test_record_common.py` - three new refusal cases
- `evidence/item9.json` - re-attestation output (regenerated)

### Test Plan
- [ ] Manual verification: re-run the body's probe (truncated `sizing.json`, stubbed provenance) on `make_record.py`; expect the exception and zero gzips.
- [ ] Automated tests: `python -m unittest sim/bitcell/lib/test_record_common.py -k RefusesBeforeWritingEvidence` (single process, local; no SPICE needed for this class); the item-9 cascade's cold-start bench run is a separate step that goes through `klt sim` per host rules, not hand-launched grids.
- [ ] Edge cases: column writer with one missing request file among eleven benches.

### Related open work
Duplicate check: none found. #151 (git_short_sha) is a different defect on the same writers, disregarded as out of scope; it may share the item-9 cascade carrier.

`A1.1` from the approved post-Phase-1 research backlog.

Part of #309.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Record runtime/deployment choice, database access ownership, polling cadence and delivery-latency objective.
- [ ] Specify bounded batches, retry/backoff, shutdown, restart recovery, and behavior when no new work is produced.
- [ ] Explain scale-to-zero and operational-cost trade-offs in an ADR/spec update; leases are conditional, not a default requirement.

## Optional user grilling before work

**Before starting work, you may invoke the `grilling` skill to clarify the decisions below with the user. If these decisions are not already settled in the linked specs or prerequisite tickets, grill the user first rather than guessing.**

Ask about intended deployment/budget and acceptable delivery latency; do not assume an always-on container is acceptable.

Record agreed answers in this ticket and the relevant specification/ADR before implementation. Downstream implementation tickets inherit the approved decisions; do not reopen settled choices without new evidence.

## Starting points

- `docs/adr/0004-transactional-outbox-http-triggered-drain.md`
- `docs/specs/cross-cutting.md`

## Scope and verification

- Inspect current implementation and existing tests before changing behavior; do not duplicate delivered work.
- Write regression tests first for correctness changes. Keep implementation bounded to this ticket and update contracts/specs alongside behavior changes.
- For affected Go modules, run `go build ./...`, `go test ./...`, and `go vet ./...`; shared `pkg/` changes require checks for dependent modules. Keep binaries in gitignored `bin/` directories.
- For HTTP/OpenAPI changes, run `make openapi-validate` and `make openapi-check`.
- For frontend changes, follow `docs/agents/web-frontend.md`, including generated-client drift checks (`npm run api:check`) and relevant unit/browser/accessibility gates.
- Changes to a service-owned database shared with a worker must cover both modules and mirrored schemas.
- Spec-only work needs a consistency review, not unrelated build/test runs. Record actual verification evidence and outstanding limitations.
